markup: Characteristics of Parliamentary system the Indian
answermarkup:
The characteristic of the Indian Parliamentary system are as follows:
i. In this system, the legislature of the Central Government is known as the Parliament. The Indian Parliament comprises of the President, the Lok Sabha and the Rajya Sabha.
ii. Members of the Lok Sabha are elected by the people through elections held at regular intervals. The total number of members in the House is fixed.
iii. All political parties contest elections and the party which gets more than half of the seats of the House is considered as the majority party. This party then forms the government.
iv. In case no party gets a clear majority, two or more than two parties come together to form a majority and establish a government. Such a government is known as coalition government.
v. Through this system, the candidates directly elected by the people become the members of the legislature and the party who wins a majority gets a chance to form the government. 
vi. Also, the leader of the majority party becomes the Prime Minister and selects the candidates for ministerial positions from his elected colleagues.
vii. The Prime Minister and the council of ministers selected by him forms the Executive in the Parliamentary system of government.

2) But, if any act of the President violates the Constitution, the Parliament has the authority to remove him.
3) This process known as process of Impeachment.
4) The procedure for impeachment is as follows:
i) Any one House can lay the charge of violation of the Constitution.
ii) The investigation of the charge is carried out by the other House.
iii) If the resolution is passed by special (2/3rd) majority of both the Houses, the President can be removed from his post.

markup: Functions of the Chief Minister
answermarkup:
The functions of the Chief Minister, as an Executive head of the state, are as follows:
(1) To form an able Council of Ministers giving maximum representation to various regions and social groups.
(2) To distribute portfolios considering the political experience, administrative skills, public awareness, leadership, etc. of the ministers.
(3) To develop proper cooperation and coordination between Departments, resolve their conflicts and make them work effectively.
(4) To lead the state, frame proper policies and implement them effectively, intervene in issues of the state and solve them for the comfort of the people.

markup: Criminal Law
answermarkup:
1) Serious crimes are dealt under Criminal law.

(4) If the charges are proved, there are provisions for severe punishment.

markup: Council of Ministers
answermarkup:
1) The Council of Ministers consists of the Chief Minister and other ministers.
(2) The leader of the majority party in Legislative Assembly is appointed as the Chief Minister by the Governor.
(3) The Governor also appoints the other ministers chosen by the Chief Minister to form Council of Ministers.
(4) Framing appropriate laws, working for the welfare of the people, governing the state efficiently are some of the functions of the Council of Ministers.
(5) The Chief Minister along with his Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to the Legislative Assembly.

markup: Vidhan Parishad of Maharashtra
answermarkup:
i. Vidhan Parishad is the second House of the Maharashtra legislature.

answermarkup:

2) He is elected by the directly elected representatives of the Central and State legislatures.

markup: Powers of the Governor
answermarkup:
The Governor enjoys certain important Legislative and Executive powers as the head of the state.
(1) The Bills passed by Vidhan Sabha and Vidhan Parishad are converted into laws only after receiving his assent.
(2) He has the right to summon the session of the state legislature and to conclude it.
(3) He can issue an ordinance to make law, on important subject if required, when the Legislature is not in session.
(4) He appoints the Chief Minister and the other Council of Ministers.

markup: No-confidence motion
answermarkup:
1) In the Parliamentary system of government, the Legislature tries to keep control over the Executive.
2) The Executive stays in power till it enjoys the support of the majority in Lok Sabha.
3) The members of the Lok Sabha can move a No-confidence motion by simply expressing "We do not have confidence in the government".
4) If the motion is passed with majority support, the Council of Ministers (the Executive) has to resign.
5) Thus, this is the most effective way to keep a check on the Council of Ministers.

answermarkup:

3) Later, a constitutional amendment was made to limit the size of the Council of Ministers.
4) As per this amendment, the number of ministers in the Council should not be more than 15% of the total number of members in the Lok Sabha.

markup: Session
answermarkup:

markup: The Governor

markup: Vidhan Sabha of Maharashtra
answermarkup:

markup: Public Interest Litigation (PIL)
answermarkup:

markup: Presidential system of government
answermarkup:

markup: Members of Parliament
answermarkup:
1) The members of Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha are known as Members of Parliament (MPs).
2) The members of Lok Sabha are directly elected by the people.
3) The members of Rajya Sabha are elected from the constituent States and Union Territories.
4) MPs try to resolve the queries and complaints of their constituencies by raising questions in the Parliament.
5) MPs also participate in the process of formulation of laws.
6) The Government allocates funds to MPs to carry out development activities in their constituencies.

markup: Bill of Law
answermarkup:
1) At the initial stage of law-making process, a rough draft of the law is prepared.
2) This rough draft or outline is known as 'draft proposal of the law' or 'bill of law'.
3) The Bill clearly mentions the objectives and the details of the proposed law.
4) Every bill has to undergo three readings in both the Houses, and then it is put to vote.

markup: Bureaucracy is considered as an important instrument of social transformation.
answermarkup:
1) Many laws are enacted by the government for empowerment of women, protection of children and marginalised sections of the society.
(2) Social change is brought through the implementation of such policies.
(3) These laws are successfully implemented by the bureaucracy.
Hence, Bureaucracy is considered as an important instrument of social transformation.

markup: The Indian judiciary has made a significant contribution in the development of the country.
answermarkup:
1) The Indian judiciary has always given importance to social values while protecting the Constitution.
(2) It has exposed wrong practices like superstitions, discrimination, injustice to weaker sections, etc. and forced the legislature to pass laws against them.
(3) It has protected individual freedom, the federal system and the Constitution of India.
(4) Common people have a lot of respect and trust in the judicial system.
Thus, the Indian judiciary has made a significant contribution in the development of the country.

markup: Coordination between the Civil Servants and Ministers help in efficient functioning of the government.
answermarkup:
1) In Parliamentary democracy, the Executive is responsible for efficient governance of the country.
(2) The decisions relating to the concerned department are made by the minister-in-charge, but necessary information to make such decisions is given by the civil servants.
(3) The ministers are dependent on the civil servants for many reasons.
Hence, coordination and mutual trust between the civil servants and ministers help in efficient functioning of the government.

markup: Judiciary in India is an integrated system.
answermarkup:
(1) India is a Union of States. The Centre and the Constituent States have a separate Legislature and Executive.
(2) But there is one judicial system for the whole of India.
(3) The Supreme Court is the apex court under which there are High Courts.
(4) The High Courts control the district courts and below them are the lower courts.
Hence, this structure makes Judiciary in India an integrated system.

markup: Though Lok Sabha is the lower House, it is more powerful than Rajya Sabha.
answermarkup:
1) Since members of Lok Sabha are directly elected by the people, it represents the people of the nation in the true sense.
2) Money bills related to financial matters are presented in Lok Sabha. Rajya Sabha has very limited powers with respect to Money Bills.
3) Since the total membership of Lok Sabha is more than Rajya Sabha, it always gets an upper hand when decisions are taken in the joint meeting of both the Houses.
4) Only Lok Sabha can pass a no-confidence motion against the Council of Ministers.
Hence, though Lok Sabha is the lower House, it is more powerful than Rajya Sabha.

markup: The Chief Minister's post is most important in the state.
answermarkup:
1) The Chief Minister can select his Council of Ministers according to his choice.
(2) He can ask any of his ministers to resign.
(3) Framing policies of public welfare and developing the state in a progressive manner entirely depends upon the Chief Minister.
(4) The Chief Minister leads the state and people look at him as a problem solver.
(5) His intervention in solving the problems of the state comforts the people.
Hence, all these executive powers makes the Chief Minister's post most important in the State.

markup: Lok Sabha is known as the first House.
answermarkup:
1) Lok Sabha is the lower and the first House of the Parliament of India.
2) Lok Sabha is the House of Representatives directly elected by the people.
Hence, Lok Sabha is known as the first House.

markup: India adopted the Parliamentary System of government.
answermarkup:
1) The Parliamentary System of government. developed primarily in England.
2) The British ruled over India for about 150 years. During this period, they ruled in accordance with this system.
3) So, Indians were familiar with this system of government.
4) The Constituent Assembly also adopted this system after a thorough discussion.
5) Hence, the framers of the Constitution made a few changes to suit the Indian situation, and adopted the Parliamentary System.

markup: The Governor is the titular/nominal head of the state.
answermarkup:
1) The Constitution has granted Executive powers to the Governor as the head of the state.
(2) The government of the state is run in the name of the Governor.
(3) But in reality, the administration is carried out by the Chief Minister.
Hence, the Governor is the titular/ nominal head of the state.

markup: Reservation policy is followed even in Civil Services.
answermarkup:
1) A part of the society comprising of Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, Women, Other Backward Castes and specially-abled is termed as the weaker section of the society.
(2) It was essential to empower these weaker sections.
(3) They were left out of civil services due to social inequality.
(4) In order to establish social justice and provide opportunities to weaker sections of the society, reservation policy is followed even in civil services.

markup: Discussions and deliberations are important in a Parliamentary System of government.
answermarkup:
1) In a Parliamentary System of government, decisions are taken after discussions and deliberations.
2) Members of the opposition party also participate in the discussions.
3) They may support the government or point out shortcomings in the government policies.
4) Laws are framed after detailed discussions on questions of public welfare. This does not happen in autocratic rule.
5) Hence, to protect the welfare and freedom of common people, discussions and deliberations are important.

markup: The President is the nominal and constitutional Head of India.
answermarkup:
1) The Constitution has vested all executive powers in the President.
2) The government carries out its functions in the name of the President.
3) However, in reality, the Prime Minister and the Council of Ministers run the government.
Hence, the President is the nominal and Constitutional Head of India.

markup: Members of the Rajya Sabha work as representatives of the constituent states.
answermarkup:
i. The Rajya Sabha is known as the Upper or the Second House.
ii. The members of the Rajya Sabha are indirectly elected.
iii. The 28 states and 9 Union Territories of the country are represented in the Rajya Sabha.
Therefore, the members of the Rajya Sabha work as representatives of the constituent states.

markup: The Parliament is of great importance in the Parliamentary System of government.
answermarkup:
1) In the Parliamentary System of government the members of the Legislature are directly elected by the people.
2) Since the elected members represent the people of the nation in the Parliament, they express and carry the hopes and carry the hopes and wishes of the people.
3) The Parliament decides the policies for the welfare of the people.
4) If the Parliament feels that the Executive does not work in accordance to its wishes, it can remove the Executive from power by passing a no-confidence motion against it.
Since, the Parliament reflects the wishes and opinions of the people of the nation, it is of great importance.

markup: Bureaucracy is an important instrument of social transformation.
answermarkup:
i. The government enacts laws for the empowerment of women, child security, plans for marginalised sections, etc.
ii. The implementation of these laws is undertaken by the bureaucracy.
iii. The implementation of these laws and policies helps to brings about a social change.
Hence, it is said that the bureaucracy is an important instrument of social transformation.

markup: The Bureaucracy is not held directly responsible for any success or failure of policy.
answermarkup:
1) It is the Minister who is responsible for the efficient and smooth functioning of his department.
(2) Though providing necessary information and giving advice is the function of the bureaucracy, it is not accountable for any inefficiency.
(3) The Parliament holds the Minister responsible for inefficiency and malpractices.
(4) In such case, the Minister bears the responsibility and protects the bureaucracy.
Thus, the anonymity of bureaucracy is preserved, which means they are not held directly responsible for any success or failure of policy.

markup: The bureaucracy is permanent in nature.
answermarkup:
i. The bureaucracy has to undertake various important tasks like tax collection, environment protection, maintenance of law & order and provisions regarding social security.
ii. Also, although the Prime Minister and the Council of Ministers and hence the ruling political may change after every election, the bureaucracy is expected to discharge its duties by remaining neutral.
Since, this requires stability, the bureaucracy has to be permanent in nature.

markup: The Council of Ministers have to resign if the No Confidence motion is passed with majority support.
answermarkup:
i. The Government stays in power till it enjoys the support of majority in the Lok Sabha.
ii. There can be a loss of majority if the members of the Parliament withdraw their support.
iii. In such a case the government cannot remain in power.
iv. A no-confidence motion in the House can be passed by the members simply saying 'we do not have confidence in the government'.
v. Thereafter, the Council of Ministers have to resign if the No Confidence motion is passed with majority support.

markup: The Constitution has made provision for independence of Judiciary.
answermarkup:
1) The Constitution wants Judiciary to work freely, without any kind of pressure.
(2) The independence of the judiciary is maintained so as to enable the judges to fearlessly carry out the function of giving justice.
For this purpose, the Constitution has made provisions for independence of Judiciary.

markup: The Council of Ministers has to take the Parliament into confidence while framing policies.
answermarkup:
1) The Council of Ministers has to decide specific policies on subject like education, agriculture, industry, health, foreign affairs, etc.
2) The Ministers of respective departments have to lay their policy plans in the House and discuss them thoroughly.
3) The policies cannot be implemented without the approval of the Parliament.
4) Also, the. Council of Ministers can stay in power till it enjoys the support of the Parliament.
5) Hence, it has to take the Parliament into confidence while framing policies.

markup: The minister bears the responsibility and protects the bureaucracy.
answermarkup:
i. Bureaucracy, is the administrative system that works under the Union Executive and is expected to carry out the implementation of their policy decisions with the efficiency and commitment. However, the success or failure of a policy cannot be linked to a civil servant.
ii. The efficient and smooth functioning of the department is the responsibility of the Minister and if there is any inefficiency the Minister would be held responsible.
iii. There can be no public criticism of the Civil Servants.
iv. If there is any malpractice, the Parliament will hold the Minister responsible for it.
Thus, the minister bears the responsibility and protects the bureaucracy.

markup: The Vidhan Parishad is a permanent House.
answermarkup:
i. The Vidhan Parishad is never fully dissolved.
ii. A fixed number of members retire every two years.
iii. Fresh elections are held for the seats that are vacated by the retiring members.
Thus, the Vidhan Parishad is a permanent House.

markup: Rajya Sabha is a permanent House.
answermarkup:
1) The tenure of the members of Rajya Sabha does not get over at the same time.
2) 1/3rd of the total membership of Rajya Sabha retire after every two years and equal number of new members get elected.
3) Because the limited members of Rajya Sabha retire step by step, it can function continuously.
Since Rajya Sabha is never dissolved completely it is called a permanent House.

markup: Vidhan Parishad (Legislative Council) is a permanent House.
answermarkup:
1) All members of the Vidhan Parishad (MLCs) do not retire at the same time.
(2) A specific number 1/3 rd of the members retire every 2 years.
(3) These vacant seats are filled again by conducting fresh elections for those seats.
(4) The tenure of each member is 6 years.
(5) Since the Vidhan Parishad is never fully dissolved, it is a permanent House.

markup: It is necessary for civil servants to be politically neutral.
answermarkup:
1) In Parliamentary democracy, in India, a new government comes in power after every five years. But the bureaucracy is permanent, i.e. they remain same.
(2) Bureaucracy is expected to implement the policies and decisions of the earlier
government with same efficiency and commitment.
(3) Civil servants are expected to keep away from taking a political stand and remain neutral while discharging their duties.
(4) If civil servants work according to their political views it will lead to chaos.
Hence, they should be politically neutral.

markup: The Judiciary of India is an integrated system
answermarkup:
i. India is a Union of States.
ii. There is a separate legislature and executive for the Centre and the Constituent States.
iii. However, the judicial system is common for the whole of India.
iv. The Centre and the Constituent States have no division of courts between them.
Thus, it can be said that, the Judiciary of India is an integrated system.

markup: The President is the nominal or constitutional head, whereas the Prime Minister is the actual head.
answermarkup:
i. The President is the Supreme Head of the State. His office is of great respect and represents the Republic of India.
ii. The Constitution has vested all executive powers to the President and all functions of the country are carried out in his name.
iii. But in reality the Prime Minister and Council of Ministers run the government.
Therefore, the President is the nominal or constitutional head, whereas the Prime Minister is the actual head.

markup: No-confidence motion is an effective tool of keeping a check over the Executive.
answermarkup:
1) In the Parliamentary System, the Executive is dependent upon the confidence of the Legislature in them.
2) If the Legislature feels that the Executive does not work in accordance to its wishes, it can pass a no-confidence motion against the Executive.
3) If the Legislature passes the no-confidence motion with a majority, then the Executive has to resign.
4) The Constitution has provided this tool to prevent the Executive from misusing its powers.
Hence, no-confidence motion is an effective tool of keeping a check over the Executive.

markup: India has 29 constituent states, but 31 Vidhan Sabha.
answermarkup:
1) According to the Constitution, every constituent state must have a Vidhan Sabha (Legislative Assembly).
(2) India has 29 constituent states and each state has its Vidhan Sabha.
(3) Out of the 7 Union Territories in India, Delhi and Puducherry have Vidhan Sabha.
Hence, India has 29 constituent states, but 31 Vidhan Sabha.

markup: Courts have played an important role in strengthening the democracy in India.
answermarkup:
i. A significant contribution has been made by the Indian judiciary towards the development of the country.
ii. The judicial system is trusted and respected by the citizens of the country.
iii. Individual freedom, federal system and the Constitution of India is protected by the judiciary.
Thus, courts have played an important role in strengthening the democracy in India.

markup: Work of the Gadar organisation
answermarkup:
i. The Gadar organisation was an important organisation setup by the Indians living in America and Canada.
ii. The word Gadar means 'revolt'. Also Gadar was the name of the journal of this organisation which acted as its mouthpiece.
iii. This journal pointed out the effects of the British rule in India and gave information about the daring deeds of the revolutionaries and thus inculcated love for the nation and gave the message of rebellion to the Indians.
iv. The leaders of the Gadar organisation decided to take advantage of the war situation and planned a revolt in Punjab against the British.
v. The Indian soldiers in the British army were persuaded to join the revolt led by Rash Bihari Bose and Vishnu Ganesh Pingle.
vi. However, due to treachery Pingle fell in the hands of the police and was hanged to death.
vii. Rash Bihari Bose managed to escape to Japan where he continued his revolutionary work.

markup: Indian Independence Act (1947)
answermarkup:
1. The Act was passed by the British Parliament on 18 July 1947.
2. It stated that India and Pakistan would become independent on 15 August 1947.
3. The British Parliament would have no control over these nations after independence.
4. The princely states were given the right to join India or Pakistan or remain independent.

markup: Poona Pact
answermarkup:
1) After the Second Round Table Conference, the British Prime Minister Ramsay Mac Donald declared Communal Awards.
(2) Communal Awards granted separate electorates to the Dalits as demanded by Dr. Ambedkar.
(3) Gandhiji was against the division on the basis of caste. He started fast unto death in Yerwada jail.
(4) The leaders of Indian National Congress requested Dr. Ambedkar to reconsider his demand in the interest of the nation.
(5) So, Dr. Babasaheb Ambedkar signed the Poona Pact with Gandhiji in 1932.
(6) It provided reserved seats instead of separate electorates for the Dalits.

markup: Vasudev Balwant Phadke
answermarkup:
1) Vasudev Balwant Phadke gave an armed struggle against the British in Maharashtra.
(2) He was of the opinion that there should be armed struggle to fight against the British.
(3) Vastad Lahuji Salve gave him training of arms.
(4) He organized Ramoshis and led armed struggle in Maharashtra, but was unsuccessful.
(5) He was sent to Eden Jail by the British Government where he died in 1883.

markup: Sir Sayyad Ahmed Khan
answermarkup:
1) Sir Sayyad Ahmad Khan worked for the cause of Muslims.
2) He believed that the Muslims would not make progress without acquiring western education and science.
3) He founded 'The Mohammedan Anglo Oriental College' which later became Aligarh Muslim University.

markup: Land Revenue Policy in India during the pre-British era
answermarkup:
i. The village economic system in India was self sufficient before the British, wherein agriculture and related services, fulfilled the needs of the villages.
ii. In the pre-British era, land revenue was not the main source of income and revenue was based on the type of crop.
iii. The farmer used to be exempted from the taxation in case of loss of crops and the revenue was collected in form of grains.
iv. Also, the land of the farmer's was not confiscated even in case of late payment of tax.

markup: The first outburst of the war of independence of 1857
answermarkup:
i. The British provided long enfield rifles to the Indian sepoys which used cartridges smeared with the fats of cows and pigs.
ii. Since, the end of these cartridges had to be bitten off, it hurt the religious sentiments of the sepoys and they refused to use the cartridges. Due to this, they had to face disciplinary action.
iii. As a reaction to this unjust nature of British officers, Mangal Pandey from Barrackpore cantonment shot an English officer, for which he was arrested and hanged to death.
iv. Thereafter, the entire regiment of Indian sepoys at Meerut took part in the freedom struggle and marched towards Delhi.
v. This march was voluntarily joined by thousands of Indians on the way towards Delhi.
vi. The protestors handed over the leadership to the Mughal Emperor Bahadur Shah and declared him as the Emperor of India.

markup: Akhil Bhartiya Kisan Sabha
answermarkup:
i. Prof. N.G. Ranga established the Akhil Bhartiya Kisan Sabha in 1936.
ii. The President of this organisation was Swami Sahajanand Saraswati.
iii. A declaration of peasants’ rights was presented to the Indian National Congress by this organisation.
iv. Thousands of peasants attended the Indian National Congress session which was held in the rural part of Faizpur in Maharashtra.

markup: Revolt of Indian Navy and Air Force
answermarkup:
1) Inspired by the heroics of the Indian National Army, the soldiers on the British warship 'Talwar' revolted on 8th  February 1946.
(2) They hoisted the tricolour flag on the ship and raised slogans against the British Government.
(3) The exchange of fire between the rebels and the British army took place.
(4) The workers and comman people extended their support.
(5) To support this uprising, the Air Force from Delhi, Lahore, Karachi, Ambala, Meerut went on strike.
(6) The naval soldiers laid down their arms after the mediation by Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel.

markup: Prarthana Samaj
answermarkup:
i. The Paramhansa Sabha formed by Dadoba Pandurang Tarkhadkar in 1848, got dissolved and some of its members founded the Prarthana Samaj with Dadoba's brother Dr. Atmaram Pandurang as its first president.
ii. While enrolment of young graduates from Mumbai University increased the prestige of the institution, its work was carried forward by Justice Ranade and Dr. R. G. Bhandarkar.
iii. The principles of the Prarthana Samaj included opposition to idol worship and rituals and acceptance of monotheism. The institution also stressed on devotion and prayers.
iv. In order to reform the society, the institution started orphanage, women's education institutes, night schools for workers and society for dalits.
v. As an attempt to solve the social problems, a member of the institution, Maharshi Vitthal Ramji Shinde established the 'Depressed Classes Mission'.

markup: Dual Government
answermarkup:
1) The British East India Company in order to consolidate rule introduced new system of governance in India known as Dual Government.
2) It was introduced by Robert Clive in Bengal in 1765 wherein the East India Company took over the revenue collection. The maintenance of law and order was the responsibility of the Nawab of Bengal.

markup: Dandi Marčh
answermarkup:
i. Dandi, a seashore, in Gujarat was chosen by Gandhiji to begin the Salt Satyagraha.
ii. He set out from Sabarmati Ashram on foot with 78 followers on 12th  March, 1930 for launching the Salt Satyagraha.
iii. On the way, Gandhiji gave speeches to the villagers in which he appealed to the people to bravely participate in the Civil Disobedience Movement.
iv. Due to his speeches, people willingly joined the Movement and it spread everywhere.
v. A distance of approximately 385 kms was covered. On 5th  April, 1930, Gandhiji along with his followers reached Dandi.
vi. On the following day, i.e., on 6th  April, 1930, he broke the Salt Act by picking up the salt from the seashore of Dandi. This led to the beginning of the Civil Disobedience Movement all over the country.

markup: Religious reforms among the Muslims
answermarkup:
i. The social reform among the Muslim community was started by Abdul Latif by establishing 'The Mohammedan Literary Society' in Bengal.
ii. Thereafter, Sir Syed Ahmad Khan established the 'The Mohammedan Anglo Oriental College', which later developed into the 'Aligarh Muslim University'.
iii. He not only advocated western science and technology, but also had a firm belief that Muslims could make progress only by studying modern education and science.

markup: Work of Swaraj Party
answermarkup:
1) The leaders of the Swaraj Party put up an idea of contesting elections and obstructing the work of the government.
2) They severely opposed unjust policies of the government.
3) They demanded that a Responsible Government should be given to India.
4) They demanded for Round Table Conference.
5) They made a resolution in Assembly which demanded the release of political leaders taken as prisoners.
6) Many resolutions were passed in the Central Legislative Assembly but were rejected by the government.

markup: Samyukta Maharashtra Parishad
answermarkup:
1) On 12 May 1946, a resolution was passed regarding Samyukta Maharashtra in the Sahitya Sammelan at Belgaon.
(2) On this background, Maharashtra Ekikaran Parishad was convened under the leadership of Shankarrao Dev at Mumbai on 28 July.
(3) A resolution was passed that all Marathi speaking regions should be united in one state.
(4) It should include the regions of Mumbai, Central provinces Marathwada and Gomantak.

markup: Ramkrishna Mission
answermarkup:
1) Swami Vivekananda, a close disciple of Ramkrishna Paramhansa, founded the Ramkrishna Mission in 1897.
2) The mission carried out social work like providing help to famine stricken people, patients and gave medical help to the poor and worked for female education.
3) It taught people service to humanity is true religion and worked towards spiritual progress of the people.

markup: Wavell Plan (1945)
answermarkup:
1. Lord Wavell, the Viceroy of India, prepared a plan in June 1945.
2. It aimed to provide equal representation to Hindus and Muslims in the Viceroy’s Executive Council.
3. It also proposed fair representation for Dalits and minorities in central and provincial legislatures.
4. The Simla Conference was held to discuss it, but it failed due to differences between Congress and the Muslim League.

markup: Commission for Reconstruction of States
answermarkup:
1) Indian Government appointed a 'Commission for Reconstruction of States' on 29 December, 1953.
(2) It was formed under the Chairmanship of Justice Fazal Ali.
(3) In the proposal presented by the commission on 10 October, 1955, a creation of bilingual Mumbai State was advocated.

markup: Cabinet Mission (1946)
answermarkup:
1. The British Prime Minister Attlee sent a Cabinet Mission to India in March 1946.
2. It consisted of three British ministers — Pethick Lawrence, Stafford Cripps, and A.V. Alexander.
3. The Mission recognized India’s right to frame its own Constitution.
4. The plan failed as Congress and the Muslim League did not fully agree with its proposals.

markup: Age of Renaissance
answermarkup:
1) Renaissance literally means rebirth or revival. In the latter phase of medieval Europe, reformation, religious reform movement and geographical discoveries gained momentum.
2) It was a comprehensive movement which touched all aspects of human life. The Greek and Roman traditions in art, architecture and philosophy were revived in the Age of Renaissance.
3) Humanitarianism got great impetus.
4) Renaissance inspired all round progress and ushered a new era in the history of world.
5) This developments took place from 13th century to 16th century in Europe. This period is known as the Age of Renaissance.

markup: Rash Behari Bose
answermarkup:
1) Rash Behari Bose was living in Japan since 1915.
(2) He had established the 'Indian Independence League' by organising the Indian patriots living in the South East Asia.
(3) Japan conquered the territories of South-East Asia controlled by the British.
(4) Rash Behari Bose, with the help of Captain Mohan Singh, formed the Indian
National Army or Azad Hind Sena from the Indian prisoners of war captured by Japan.

markup: Commercialisation of Agriculture
answermarkup:
1) In the pre-British period, farmers used to cultivate food grains to fulfill domestic need as well as need of the village.
2) The British government gave encouragements to the cultivation of cash crops like indigo, cotton, tobacco, tea, etc.
3) The shift from cultivation of foodgrains to profit-yielding cash crops is known as Commercialisation of Agriculture.

markup: Worker's Movement at Ahmedabad
answermarkup:
i. The First World War had led to an increase in prices of goods.
ii. Hence, the mill workers demanded for a hike in salary. But the mill owners did not accept this demand.
iii. Therefore, as per Gandhiji's advice, the mill workers went on hunger strike.
iv. Finally, the mill owners surrendered to the demands of the workers and their salary was increased.

markup: Development of transport and communication by British in India
answermarkup:
i. The British developed modern facilities like transport and communication to facilitate trade as well as for the convenience of administration.
ii. They introduced railway transport in India and the first train ran from Mumbai to Thane in 1853.
iii. The British started the Telegraph system in India in the same year. This led to a good connectivity between all cities and military stations.
iv. They also started the Postal system.
v. This development in transport and communication impacted the social life of Indian on large scale and brought a sense of unity among them.

markup: The Round Table Conference
answermarkup:
1) The British Prime Minister, Ramsay Mac donald wanted to discuss constitutional issues related to India.
(2) For this purpose, he organised Three Round Table Conferences at London between 1930 and 1932.
(3) Representatives of various communities, castes, political parties and princely states attended the conferences.
(4) Gandhiji attended the Second Round Table Conference as the representative of Indian National Congress.
(5) As no important decision was taken in them, all these conferences proved to be futile.

markup: Land Revenue Policy in India during the British era
answermarkup:
i. The British made several changes in the land revenue system in India.
ii. The area of the land was measured and the tax was fixed according to this area.
This tax had to be paid compulsorily in form of cash and in case of failure of payment, the land of the farmer would be confiscated.
iv. Also, the British system of land revenue differed from place to place. This led to the exploitation of the farmers.

markup: Contribution of Swami Dayanand Saraswati
answermarkup:
i. Swami Dayanand Saraswati founded the Arya Samaj in 1875, whose slogan was 'Go Back to Vedas'.
ii. He wrote the book 'Satyarth Prakash' which was a commentary on Vedas. In this book he stated that ancient vedic religion was true religion and had no place for casteism.
iii. He also promoted gender equality.
iv. Arya Samaj had branches all over India and it helped to establish many educational institutions.

markup: Gandhi-Irwin Pact
answermarkup:
1) On the appeal of the Prime Minister, the Viceroy released Gandhiji and other political leaders from prison.
(2) In this conducive atmosphere, a pact was signed between Gandhiji and Viceroy Irwin. It is known as Gandhi-Irwin Pact.
(a) According to the pact, the British Government gave an assurance of providing Responsible Government in the proposed constitution of India.
(b) Congress decided to withdraw the Civil Disobedience Movement.
(c) Agreed to participate in the Second Round Table Conference.

markup: Museums and History
answermarkup:
1) A place where ancient artefacts, paintings, photographs, tools, coins, documents, clothes, etc. are exhibited is known as Museum.
2) Ancient artefacts give us information about the economic, social, political and religious conditions of the respective periods.
3) The metal and the inscriptions on the coin tell us about the economic conditions of that period and the metals used.
4) We come to know progress in art of making tools, paintings, sculpture and metallurgy.
5) History and museums are related. They are important source of writing history.

markup: Nagpur Pact, 1953
answermarkup:
i. The purpose of signing the Nagpur Pact in 1953, was to make the Marathi people of all regions resolve to make one state.
ii. A Samyukta Maharashtra was formed according to this pact, which included Western Maharashtra, Vidarbha along with Marathwada.
iii. The various assurances given by the Nagpur Pact are;
a. Equitable financial provision of developmental work
b. Ample finance for technical and vocational education
c. Provision of state government services in regions according to its population
d. Assembly Session once every year in Nagpur

markup: Paika Rebellion
answermarkup:
1) There were many independent kingdoms in Odisha in the medieval period.
2) The kings used to have a standing army known as Paikas.
3) The kings gave them rent free land for their cultivation and livelihood.
4) In return, they were supposed to fight along with the king in case of any war.
5) The English conquered Odisha in 1803 and took over the hereditary rent free lands granted to the Paikas.
6) This resulted in armed rebellion of the Paikas against the British under the leadership Bidyadhar. of Bakshi Jaganbandhu

markup: Colonialism
answermarkup:
1) Exploitation of one country by another and making it into a colony is called Colonialism.
2) On the basis of economic and military strength one country occupies region of another country and establishes its political supremacy.
3) Many European nations established their colonies in various parts of the continents of America, Asia, Africa and Australia.
4) They grabbed the power by using force to exploit the colonies systematically.
This gave rise to Imperialism.

markup: Reforms of Rajarshi Shahu Maharaj in the state of Kolhapur
answermarkup:
1) Rajarshi Shahu Maharaj worked for abolishing of caste discrimination.
(2) He made revolutionary declaration for reservation in the state of Kolhapur.
(3) He made law for free and compulsory primary education.
(4) He worked to remove restrictions on inter dining, inter marriage and change of occupation in the caste system.
(5) He passed the Act of inter caste marriage and made it legal in state.
(6) He abolished 'Balutedari System', by publishing a declaration in the Government Gazette of the state of Kolhapur on 22 February, 1918.
(7) This allowed people to practice any occupation and freed them from type of social slavery.

markup: Revolutionary work of Vasudev Balwant Phadke
answermarkup:
i. Vasudev Balwant Phadke was a revolutionary from Maharashtra who took up armed struggle against the British for independence of India.
ii. In order to achieve this, he took training of arms from Vastad Lahuji Salve.
iii. He also organised the Ramoshis and revolted against the British. However, this rebellion became unsuccessful.
iv. Thereafter, he was sent to the Eden Jail where he died in 1883.

markup: Four Point Programme of the Indian National Congress
answermarkup:
In the session of 1906 of the Indian National Congress, the four point programme was unanimously accepted.
1) Swadeshi: To make use of capital, resources, manpower in our country so that it becomes self-sufficient.
2) Boycott: It was decided to boycott foreign goods as a first step, and boycott of foreign rule be the next step. It would be an attack on the roots of British imperialism.
3) Swaraj: The final objective is to attain freedom.
4) National Education: To impart education which will create pride for the nation among people.

markup: Social Work of Maharshi Vitthal Ramji Shinde
answermarkup:
1) The goal of Maharshi Vitthal Ramji Shinde was to make the Dalits self respectful, well educated and engaged in work.
(2) He worked to destroy the delusive ideas regarding Dalits in the minds of the upper caste.
(3) He founded the 'Depressed Classes Mission' for the progress of Dalits in 1906.
(4) To achieve this, he started Marathi schools and work schools in parts of Parel, Deonar in Mumbai.
(5) He actively took part in various movement which were related to the welfare of the Dalits like Satyagraha for entry in Parvati temple at Pune, Shetkari Parishad of Dalits and Federal Electorates.

markup: Films
answermarkup:
i. Films, which are considered as a unique discovery of modern technology, are an important video and audio-visual source of history.
ii. A great development took place in the development of filmmaking technique in the 20th century.
iii. Dada Saheb Phalke laid the foundation of Indian film industry in 1913.
iv. Audio-visual recordings of several historical events like Dandi Yatra, Salt Satyagraha, Quit India Movement, etc., are available.
v. These recordings enable one to see and understand the events of the past.

markup: Gandhiji's work in South Africa
answermarkup:
1) In 1893, Gandhiji went to South Africa for some legal work where he began his political work.
2) Many Indians had settled in South Africa for the purpose of trade and business.
3) They were treated as criminals and humiliating treatment was given to them.
4) Many restrictions were imposed on their freedom like it was compulsory for them to carry an identity card.
5) Gandhiji adopted the path of Satyagraha and gained justice for them.

markup: Nehru Report
answermarkup:
1) Berkenhead, the Secretary of State of India, criticised that Indian leaders were incapable of drafting a unanimously accepted constitution for India.
2) This challenge was taken up by all party committee under the chairmanship of Pandit Motilal Nehru.
3) The proposals of the Nehru Report were: 
i) implement Adult Franchise system in India, 
ii) establish self government colonies of India, and (iii) division of provinces on linguistic division.

markup: Direct Action Day (1946)
answermarkup:
1. The Muslim League declared 16 August 1946 as ‘Direct Action Day’.
2. It was called to demand the creation of a separate Muslim nation, Pakistan.
3. The day led to violent Hindu-Muslim riots in many parts of India, especially in Noakhali (Bengal).
4. Mahatma Gandhi visited Noakhali to restore peace and harmony.

markup: Prarthana Samaj
answermarkup:
1) Paramhansa Sabha was dissolved and some of its members formed Prarthana Samaj.
2) Dr. Atmaram Pandurang was its first President.
3) They opposed idol worship, monotheism and advocated prayers and devotional songs instead of rituals in place of worship of God.
4) The important contribution of Prarthana Samaj in reforming the society was that it started orphanage, women's education institutes, night schools for workers and society for Dalits.
5) The prestige of Prarthana Samaj rose immensely due to the enrollment of young graduates from Mumbai University.
6) Justice Ranade, Dr. R. G. Bhandarkar carried the work of Prarthana Samaj forward.

markup: Imperialism
answermarkup:
1) Imperialism means a powerful country controls other country by establishing its overall domination.
2) The objective of imperialism is to establish more and more colonies.
3) European countries with strong military power and imperialist aspirations enslaved the countries in Asia and Africa.
4) Imperialism gained momentum after industrial revolution and came to an end in twentieth century.

markup: Contribution of Samyukta Maharashtra Samiti
answermarkup:
Samyukta Maharashtra Samiti contributed in the following way to form Samyukta Maharashtra.
(l) Samyukta Maharashtra movement spread throughout the state and reached in rural areas.
(2) Common people also joined the movement spontaneously.
(3) When it was clear that Mumbai will not be included in Maharashtra, Samiti held demonstrations to protest and arouse public agitation.
(4) The grand success of Samyukta Maharashtra Samiti in Lok Sabha, Vidhan Sabha and Mumbai Municipal Corporation in 1957 made it clear that the voters were in favour of Samyukta Maharashtra.
(5) The agitations led by Samyukta Maharashtra Samiti during the visit of Prime Minister Pandit Jawaharlal Nehru made the approach of Central Government favourable in the formation of Maharashtra state.

markup: Mountbatten Plan (1947)
answermarkup:
1. Lord Mountbatten was appointed the Viceroy of India to oversee the transfer of power.
2. He proposed a plan for partition of India into two nations — India and Pakistan.
3. The Congress opposed partition but accepted it helplessly to avoid civil war.
4. This plan became the basis for the Indian Independence Act of 1947.

markup: Champaran Satyagraha
answermarkup:
1) The farmers in Champaran region in Bihar were forced to cultivate indigo.
2) The cultivators suffered as they received a fixed amount as price from the plantation owners.
3) In 1917, Gandhiji went to Champaran and organized the farmers.
4) He launched agitation by adopting the technique of Satyagraha.
5) The farmers were given justice and thus Gandhiji was successful in his first satyagraha in India.

markup: Objectives of the Indian National Congress
answermarkup:
The Indian National Congress was established in 1885 with the following objectives:
1) To bring together the people of India on a common platform.
2) To create a feeling of unity among them, irrespective of religion, race, language, geographical territories. 
3) To provide opportunities to understand one another's problems and views.
4) To increase the feeling of unity among the people.
5) To take measures for the upliftment of the country.

markup: Hindustan Socialist Republican Army
answermarkup:
i. Hindustan Socialist Republican Army was a wing of the revolutionary organisation Hindustan Socialist Republican Association.
ii. The main work of this army was to gather arms and execute the programmes planned by the Hindustan Socialist Republican Association.
iii. Chandrashekhar Azad was the chief of this wing and he along with the other members of the wing carried out many revolutionary activities, as follows:
a. Bhagat Singh and Rajguru filled an officer Saunders by firing bullets at him in order to avenge the death of Lala Lajpat Rai.
b. Bhagat Singh and Batukeshwar Dutt threw bombs in the Central Legislative Assembly to oppose two bills of the Government which curtailed the civil rights.

markup: Morley-Minto Reform Act (1909)
answermarkup:
i. The Indians were not satisfied with the work of the British government.
ii. According to the Indians, India was poor due to the economic policies of the British.
iii. The oppressive policy of Lord Curzon, exclusion of the educated Indians in government services and Britain's unjust behaviour towards Indians in Africa created dissatisfaction among the people.
iv. So, to satisfy the Indian people temporarily, the British passed the Morley-Minto Reform Act in 1909.
v. According to this Act, the number of Indian members in the Legislative Assembly was increased, provision was made for the inclusion of some elected Indian representatives in the Legislative Assembly and separate electorates were provided to the Indian Muslims.
vi. However, this Act sowed the seeds of division among the people of India.

markup: Kheda Satyagraha
answermarkup:
i. The crops in the Kheda district of Gujarat had failed due to constant famines.
ii. However, the government forcibly collected the land tax from the farmers.
iii. On Gandhiji's suggestion, the farmers began a movement for the scraping of tax at Kheda in 1918.
iv. Later, Gandhiji undertook the leadership of this movement and within a short period of time, the British government suspended the tax in the Kheda district.

markup: The Meerut Conspiracy Case
answermarkup:
1) The young communist leaders built militant organisations of workers and peasants.
(2) The growing influence of Communism on Indian youth became a matter of concern for the British and they felt it was α danger.
(3) The communist leaders Shripad Amrut Dange, Muzaffar Ahmed, Keshav Neelkanth Joglekar, etc. were arrested.
(4) They were falsely charged with planning of α conspiracy to overthrow the British rule.
(5) The trial took place at Meerut. So it was called as 'Meerut Conspiracy Case'.
(6) They were given different punishments.

markup: Work of Rakhmabai Janardan Save
answermarkup:
1) Dr. Rakhmabai Janardhan Save was the first practising woman doctor in India.
(2) She delivered lectures on health related issues of women.
(3) She opened a branch of Red Cross Society at Rajkot.

markup: Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel and Integration of Princely States
answermarkup:
1. After independence, more than 600 princely states existed in India.
2. Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel, the Home Minister, led the integration process.
3. He prepared the ‘Instrument of Accession’, convincing rulers to join India.
4. Except Junagad, Hyderabad, and Kashmir — all other states merged peacefully.

markup: Provincial Cabinets
answermarkup:
1) According to the Act of 1935, working of the British administered provinces were transferred to the elected representatives.
(2) Although not satisfied with the act, Congress contested elections to the Provincial Legislatures of eleven provinces in 1937.
(3) Indian National Congress gained majority in eight provinces.
(4) Congress ministries did α lot of useful work for the benefit of the people.
(5) As the British government refused their demand of Independence the Congress ministries resigned in November 1939.

markup: Literary and Social work of Swctantryaveer Savarkar
answermarkup:
1) When Swatantryaveer Savarkar was detained in the Ratnagiri jail, he started many social movements such as removal of caste differences, removal of untouchability, common dining, purification of language, etc.
(2) In his autobiography, 'Majhi Janmathep' he wrote about his experiences of the terrible days in Andaman where he spent ten years.
(3) He wrote the book "The Indian War of Independence 1857^' in which he stated 1857 rebellion as the first war of independence.
(4) He wrote an inspiring biography of Joseph Mazzini.
(5) Savarkar was a great writer, social worker and revolutionary.

markup: Carnatic Wars
answermarkup:
1) There was competition among the European nationals to secure monopoly of trading rights in India.
2) Due to this three Carnatic wars were fought between England and France.
3) England defeated France in the third Carnatic War.
4) After this, there was no strong European competitor for British East India Company in India.

markup: Problem of Kashmir
answermarkup:
1. The ruler Hari Singh wanted to keep Kashmir independent after 1947.
2. Pakistan-backed intruders attacked Kashmir in October 1947.
3. Hari Singh signed the Instrument of Accession, and Indian troops defended Kashmir.
4. India regained most of the territory, but some part remained under Pakistan’s control.

markup: Kakori Conspiracy
answermarkup:
1) After Gandhiji suspended Civil Disobedience, many youngsters like Chandrashekhar Azad, Ram Prasad Bismil, Yogesh Chatterjee, Sachindra Nath Sanyal got diverted to revolutionary ways.
(2) On 9th  August, 1925 they looted the Government treasury that was on a train near Kakori railway station in Uttar Pradesh.
(3) However, due to the immediate action of the government the revolutionaries were arrested and put on trial.
(4) Ashfaqulla Khan, Ram Prasad Bismil, Roshan Singh, Rajendra Lahiri were hanged.
(5) Chandrashekhar Azad managed to escape.

markup: Nehru Report
answermarkup:
i. When the Simon Commission arrived in India in 1928, it was boycotted by the Indians because not a single Indian was included in the Commission.
ii. So, the Secretary of State for India, Lord Birkenhead challenged the Indian leaders to draft a unanimously accepted Constitution for India.
iii. The political leaders accepted this challenge and an All-Party Committee was formed to draft the Constitution. Pandit Motilal Nehru was the chairman of this Committee.
iv. This Committee prepared the draft Constitution which was called as the 'Nehru Report'.
v. Proposals like establishing self-government in the colonies of India, implementing Adult Franchise system, dividing the provinces on linguistic basis, etc. were put forth in this report.
vi. Moreover, by the end of 1929, it was indicated that if the Nehru Report was not accepted by the government then the civil disobedience movement will be started.

markup: The Lucknow Pact
answermarkup:
1) An attempt was made under the leadership of Lokmanya Tilak to resolve differences in the Indian National Congress at its Lucknow session in 1916.
2) In the same year, there was an agreement between Indian National Congress and the Muslim League, known as the Lucknow Pact.
3) According to this Pact, Indian National Congress agreed to separate electorate for Muslims.
4) In return, the Muslim League agreed to support the Indian National Congress in Bits work for getting political rights to India.

markup: Queen's Proclamation post freedom struggle of 1857
answermarkup:
i. After the struggle of 1857, Queen Victoria of England issued a Declaration which was addressed to the people of India.
ii. It mentioned that, all Indians were England's progeny.
iii. It also assured that there would be no discrimination on the basis of race, religion, caste or birth place and that Government services will be given on merit.
iv. It also gave an assurance that there won't be any interference in religious matters.
v. The declaration made clear that the British crown will honour all treaties and agreements made with the rulers of the princely states by the East India Company and that no princely state would be annexed thereafter.

markup: Explain the concept : Oral Sources
answermarkup:
1) The compositions which are passed on from one generation to the other by way of information or rote leaming and which are not in written form are called the 'oral sources of history'.
2) Folk songs, powadas, ovees, inspirational songs, folk tales, etc. are included in oral sources.
3) The creators of the oral sources mostly remain unknown.
4) We come to know about prevalent social life, traditions, customs, language, etc. through oral sources.
5) The aim of oral sources was to entertain, inspire and create vitality in the society.

markup: Capitalism
answermarkup:
1) Many traders participated in the competition for trade with Asia after the discovery of the new sea routes to the east.
2) As it was not possible to carry out trade single-handedly, it was decided by the traders to pool their resources to raise capital for trade.
3) Many trading companies like the East India Company were formed.
4) Trade with Oriental countries was very profitable and responsible for economic prosperity.
5) The ruling powers gave protection and trade concessions to these companies.
6) This led to the accumulation of wealth in Europe. This wealth was used as capital for trade and commerce which gave rise to capitalism in Europe.

markup: Jungle Satyagraha
answermarkup:
i. Gandhiji launched the Civil Disobedience Movement in 1930 by breaking the Salt Act.
ii. However, where there were no salt-pans, the forest laws were broken.
iii. The tribal people, in large numbers participated in this Satyagraha.
iv. In Maharashtra, the jungle satyagrahas were carried out at Bilashi, Sangamner, Kalwan, Chirner and Pusad.

markup: Hyderabad Mukti Sangram
answermarkup:
1. Hyderabad was the largest princely state ruled by the autocratic Nizam.
2. Swami Ramananda Tirth led the movement with leaders like Narayan Reddy and Govindbhai Shroff.
3. The Nizam supported Pakistan; his associate Kasim Rizvi formed the violent ‘Razakar’ organisation.
4. India launched ‘Operation Polo’ (13–17 September 1948) — the Nizam surrendered and Hyderabad merged with India.

markup: Parliamentary Laws
answermarkup:
i. The Regulating Act of 1773 changed the title of the Bengal Governor as the Governor General and made Lord Warren Hastings, the Governor General of India.
ii. This gave him the rights to control the policies of Mumbai and Madras province and also got a committee of four members to assist him.
iii. The Pitt's India Act passed in 1784, provided for the appointment of a permanent Board of Control for better regulation and management of affairs of the East India Company in India.
iv. Also, the Parliament passed several new laws in the years 1813, 1833 and 1853, to make several changes in the working of the East India Company.
v. Thus the British Government gained an indirect control of the administration of East India Company. Also, this emergence of the British rule led to the development of the new administrative system in India.

markup: Civil Services
answermarkup:
1) There was a need of bureaucrats to strengthen the British rule in India.
2) Lord Cornwallis introduced Civil Services which became an important part of the British government.
3) The territories occupied by the British were divided into districts for administrative convenience. The district administration was headed by Collector.
4) The officers appointed through the Civil Services (ICS) were taken into administrative services.

markup: Jallianwala Bagh Incident
answermarkup:
i. The anti Rowlatt Act movement gained. momentum in several towns of the Punjab and Amritsar became the centre of this movement.
ii. General Dyer had issued orders which prohibited public meetings in the towns of Amritsar.
iii. Gandhiji was not allowed to enter the province of Punjab. Important leaders like Dr. Satyapal and Dr. Kitchlew were arrested for their involvement in the Amritsar Hartal Case.
iv. On 13th April, 1919, at Amritsar in the Jallianwala Bagh, a large but unarmed crowd had gathered to protest against the arrest of their popular leaders.
v. In order to terrorise the people, General Dyer arrived with the armed force at the Bagh. The Bagh was enclosed from all sides and had only one small gate.
vi. General Dyer surrounded the Bagh with his army and closed down the only gate. Without giving any prior notification, Dyer ordered his soldiers to open fire on the unarmed crowd. They fired till their ammunition was exhausted.
vii. In this massacre, large number of men and women were killed. After firing, as curfew was imposed, immediate treatment could not be given to the wounded. Later, military law was enforced in Punjab and many were sent to jail by the government.
viii. As a protest against this incident, Rabindranath Tagore renounced the title of 'Sir' awarded to him by the British government.
ix. Later, the 'Hunter Commission' was appointed by the British government to enquire about the incident.

markup: Dar Commission
answermarkup:
1) The President of Constituent Assembly, Dr. Rajendra Prasad established the Dar Commission on 17 June, 1947.
(2) The Commission started the work under the leadership of Justice S. K. Dar to form states on linguistic basis.
(3) On 10 December, 1948, the report of Dar Commission was published but the issue remained unsolved.

markup: Leonardo-da-Vinci
answermarkup:
1) Leonardo-da-Vinci is regarded as an all round personality of the Renaissance period.
2) He was well versed with the different branches of science and art.
3) He had mastery over varied subjects such as mathematics, astronomy, etc. sculpture, architecture, engineering, music, astronomy etc.
4) But he became world famous as a painter.
5) His paintings 'Monalisa' and 'The Last Supper' became immortal.

markup: Contribution of Marathwada in Hyderabad Liberation
answermarkup:
1. Leaders like Swami Ramananda Tirth, Govindbhai Shroff, and Anant Bhalerao played a major role.
2. The ‘Vande Mataram’ movement involved many students in the struggle.
3. Many martyrs like Govind Pansare, Ved Prakash, and Bahirji Shinde sacrificed their lives.
4. 17 September is celebrated as ‘Marathwada Mukti Din’ to mark this victory.

markup: Mulshi Satyagraha
answermarkup:
i. The farmers of Mulshi Taluka in Pune district launched a Satyagraha against the government during the Non-co-operation movement.
ii. It was done under the leadership of Senapati Pandurang Mahadev Bapat.
For doing so, he was punished by being imprisoned for six years.

markup: American War of Independence
answermarkup:
i. England had established thirteen colonies on the East Coast of America.
ii. When the English Parliament laid oppressive restrictions and taxes on these American colonies, the people revolted against it.
iii. In order to suppress these colonies, England immediately declared war.
iv. The American colonies organised the army under the leadership of George Washington and defeated England.
v. This event is known as the American War of Independence. In World history, among the political revolutions, it occupies a important place. very
vi. After winning over England, a new nation known as the United States of America, with a federal government, written constitution and which was based on the, principles of Democracy, came into existence.

markup: Home Rule Movement
answermarkup:
1) Home rule means self-rule or self-government.
2) It was modelled after the Home Rule Movement in Ireland.
3) It was led by Dr. Annie Besant and Lokmanya Tilak.
4) They made extensive tours in different parts of the country so that the demand of self-government could reach the common people.

markup: The Battle of Buxar
answermarkup:
1) Mir Kasim was replaced by Mir Jafar when he tried to put restrictions on illegal practices of the British.
2) Mir Kasim, the deposed Nawab of Bengal, Shuja-ud-Daulah, the Nawab of Ayodhya and Mughal Emperor Shah Alam formed an alliance.
3) They undertook a campaign to restrain the activities of the British in Bengal.
4) They were defeated by the British in the Battle of Buxar in 1764 in Bihar.
5) The Treaty of Allahabad was signed after the Battle of Buxar. The British secured the right to collect revenue from Bengal province by this treaty.

markup: First session of Indian National Congress
answermarkup:
1) The founding session of the Indian National Congress took place on 28th December, 1885 at Gokuldas Tejpal Sanskrit school in Mumbai.
2) It was presided by Wyomesh Chandra Banerjee, a renowned lawyer from Kolkata.
3) It was attended by seventy-two delegates from different provinces of India.
4) Allen Octavian Hume took the initiative in establishing of the Indian National Congress. 
5) Increase in the number of Indians in the administration, reduction in military expenditure were the demands placed before the British government.

markup: The Anushilan Samiti
answermarkup:
i. A revolutionary organisation called Anushilan Samiti with more than 500 branches was active in Bengal.
ii. Barindrakumar Ghosh was the chief of this organisation which received counsel and guidance from his brother Aurobindo Ghosh.
iii. Anushilan Samiti had a bomb manufacturing centre at Maniktala near Kolkata.
iv. In 1908, an attempt to kill a judge named Kingsford by Khudiram Bose and Prafulla Chaki, the members of Anushilan Samiti, became unsuccessful when they mistakenly bombed a vehicle carrying two English women.
v. Thereafter, Prafulla Chaki shot himself with a bullet and Khudiram Bose was caught by the police. Further investigations, helped police to get information about the working of Anushilan Samiti and it arrested more members including Aurobindo Ghosh. While other members were sentenced to long terms of imprisonment, Aurobindo Ghosh was set free as the court could not associate him with manufacturing of bombs.

markup: JVP Committee
answermarkup:
i. A committee was appointed by the Congress government, to study the conditions of creating linguistic provinces.
ii. This committee included Jawaharlal Nehru, Vallabhbhai Patel and Pattabhi Sitaramayya, whose initials gave this committee the name JVP committee.
iii. After completing its study, the committee submitted its report which suggested that although Congress accepted the concept of linguistic states in principle, the time for the formation of such states was not proper.
iv. This report drew a very strong response against it, from across Maharashtra. At the same time, Senapati Bapat organised rallies for awakening of the people.

markup: Servants of India Society
answermarkup:
1) Gopal Krishna Gokhale founded the Servants of India Society in 1905.
2) Its main objectives were: 
i) to create love for the county, 
ii) teach them sacrifice of self-interest, 
iii) no differentiation on the basis of caste and religion, 
iv) to create social harmony, 
v) to spread education.

markup: Struggle for Liberation of Goa
answermarkup:
1. Goa was under Portuguese rule even after India’s independence.
2. Leaders like Dr. T. B. Kunha and Dr. Ram Manohar Lohia led protests and Satyagrahas.
3. In 1954, the Azad Gomantak Dal liberated Dadra and Nagar Haveli.
4. Finally, in December 1961, the Indian Army freed Goa — ending Portuguese rule completely.

markup: Rebellion of Umaji Naik
answermarkup:
1) Exploitation was on a large scale during the Company's rule in India. There was rising discontent among the Indians. Sanyasis-Fakirs rebelled in the Bengal province.
2) Umaji Naik organised the Ramoshis and the local youth and gave a strong fight to the British in Maharashtra.
3) They drafted a declaration and appealed to the people to support them in their fight against to overthrow the British government.
4) People in Ahmednagar, Satara, Pune, Nasik, Solapur and Bhor were inspired by them.
5) Umaji Naik was arrested and hanged to death in 1832 at Pune.

markup: Dharasana Satyagraha
answermarkup:
i. Sarojini Naidu led the Satyagraha at Dharasana in Gujarat.
ii. When the satyagrahis came forward to break the Salt Act, the police resorted to lathi charge.
iii. The blows of the lathis were silently tolerated by the satyagrahis and when they were taken away for medical aid, another batch of satyagrahis replaced them. This continued endlessly.

markup: Extremists
answermarkup:
1) The leaders of the Indian National Congress who advocated intensification of the struggle to attain freedom were known as Extremists.
2) Moderates and Extremists were unanimous about the objectives of Congress. The Extremists had no faith in the constitutional methods of the Moderates.
3) According to Extremists, freedom will be attained only if lakhs of people participated in the freedom movement and challenge the British government.

markup: Merger of French Colonies
answermarkup:
i. The French were in the possession of the regions of Chandranagar, Puduchcheri, Karaikal, Mahe and Yanam even after India's independence.
ii. The Indian natives of these regions wanted to get merged with India.
iii. Also, the Indian government demanded that these territories being a part of India, should be handed over to it.
iv. In a plebiscite held by France in 1949 in Chandranagar, the people voted for India.
v. Thereafter, France first handed over Chandranagar and then other territories to the Government of India.

markup: Poorna Swaraj
answermarkup:
i. Young leaders like Pandit Nehru and Subhash Chandra Bose were not willing to accept the objective of Indian National Congress of Dominion Status. Instead, they demanded 'Complete Independence' i.e., Poorna Swaraj.
ii. Therefore, in the Lahore session of the Indian National Congress, the resolution of Poorna Swaraj was passed by the Congress.
iii. Through this resolution, the Indian National Congress gave up the objective of dominion status and declared that the objective of the National Movement was complete independence of India.
iv. On 31st December 1929, the tricolour flag was unfurled by Pandit Nehru and a resolution was passed in which 26th January was to be celebrated as Independence Day.
v. Accordingly, on 26th January, 1930, people all over India, took the pledge of carrying out the national movement in a non - violent way.

markup: Individual Satyagraha
answermarkup:
i. The Indian National Congress decided to start an anti-war propaganda since the British government constantly neglected its demands.
ii. To carry this out, it was decided that every single person should disobey the laws instead of a collective movement.
iii. This was known as 'Individual Satyagraha' and Acharya Vinoba Bhave was the first satyagrahi.
iv. Nearly 25,000 satyagrahis followed him who were sent to jail for taking part in Individual Satyagraha.

markup: Photographs
answermarkup:
1) Before the invention of photography, paintings were an important source of history. But the authenticity of such paintings is doubtful.
2) Photographs are considered more reliable, as the lens capture the persons, events and objects exactly as they appear.
3) The photograph of a person gives information about the physical features, dressing style, etc.
4) Photographs enable us to recreate visual image of an event. The photograph of object or an structure helps in understanding its nature.
Hence, photographs are important visual source of modern Indian history.

markup: Powada
answermarkup:
i. Powada is a dramatic narration of the deeds of heroic men and women in a forceful and inspiring manner. It is done by alternatively reciting poetry and prosaic extracts.
ii. It is an important oral source of history as it gives information about a historical event or the work of a person.
iii. Various Powadas were composed on the freedom struggle of 1857, valour of revolutionaries during British rule, etc. They created motivation and spirit among people.
iv. Powadas based on the work of Satyashodhak Samaj were composed to create awakening among oppressed people.
v. Apart from this, Powadas were composed on other events and movements like the Samyukta Maharashtra movement, etc.

markup: Moderate leaders
answermarkup:
i. During the early ten years, after the establishment of Indian National Congress, the Moderate leaders contributed slowly but consistently to the freedom struggle.
ii. These leaders were realistic and highly educated.
iii. To build a strong foundation, they did organised work.
iv. The values of liberalism, liberty, fraternity and equality greatly impacted them.
v. They believed in constitutional methods in getting their demands fulfilled.
vi. Gopal Krishna Gokhale, Pherozeshah Mehta, and Surendranath Banerjee were some important moderate leaders.

markup: Moderates
answermarkup:
1) The Moderates were the leaders who wanted to carry out nationalistic movement within the constitutional methods and peaceful means.
2) The leaders were realistic and highly educated and had faith in the justice of the British.
3) They had hope that if they place their demands in constitutional manner the British will give justice to their demands.
4) They were aware that a strong foundation needs to be built through organised work.
5) The philosophy and principles of western thinkers like liberalism, freedom, equality, fraternity influenced them.

markup: India House
answermarkup:
i. India House in London was an important centre which provided assistance to the Indian revolutionary movement.
ii. Pandit Shyamji Krishna Varma, had established the India House, through which Indian youths were given scholarships for higher education in England. Swatantryaveer Savarkar was one such person who had received scholarship.
iii. Another revolutionary of this organisation, Madam Cama, raised the issue of India's independence at the World Socialist Conference held at Stuggart in. Germany and unfurled the flag of India.
iv. Madanlal Dhingra, another revolutionary associated with the organisation, killed the British Officer Curzon Wylie, for which he was hanged to death.

markup: Congress Socialist Party (1934)
answermarkup:
i. Many of the young activists in the Indian National Congress realised that it was important to restructure the society on the principle of economic and social equality.
ii. They also felt that in order to protect the interests of the people, the British rule should be overthrown from India.
iii. This realisation led to the rise and growth of socialist ideology. The socialist youths decided to form the socialist party within the Indian National Congress while they were in prison at Nasik.
iv. Finally in 1934, they formed the Congress Socialist Party.
v. Acharya Narendra Dev, Jayprakash Narayan, Minu Masani, Dr. Ram Manohar Lohia, etc. were the leaders of this party and they were in the forefront during the Quit India Movement of 1942.

markup: Poona Pact
answermarkup:
i. After the Second Round Table Conference, Ramsay Mac Donald, the British Prime Minister, declared the 'Communal Award' which granted separate electorates for the Dalits.
ii. Gandhiji protested the granting of separate electorate on the basis of caste and went on fast unto death at the Yerwada jail in Poona.
iii. As Dr. Babasaheb Ambedkar represented the Dalits, he was requested by the leaders of the Indian National Congress to rethink about the demand for separate electorates.
iv. Dr. Ambedkar accepted the request for the wellbeing of the nation.
v. Hence, a pact was signed between Mahatma Gandhi and Dr. Babasaheb Ambedkar in 1932 which came to be known as the 'Poona Pact'.
vi. By this pact, a provision for reserved seats was made instead of separate electorates for the Dalits.

markup: Importance of the Quit India Movement
answermarkup:
i. The Quit India Movement also called as 'August Kranti' which started in 1942 had later become a nationwide agitation.
ii. In order to achieve independence, lakhs of Indians made endless sacrifices. Many sacrificed their lives. Even school children participated in it and children like Shirishkumar, Laldas, Dhansukhlal, Shashidhar and Ghanashyam became martyrs.
iii. The Navy, Army and the Air Force which formed the backbone of the British power also opposed the British.
iv. Large number of people participated in the movement and the number was so huge that even all the prisons in the country were not enough to contain them.
v. The agitators received enthusiasm because of the patriotic songs composed by Sane Guruji, Rashtrasant Tukdoji Maharaj, etc.
vi. Due to the Quit India Movement, the British Government realised that the discontent of the Indian people against them had reached a climax and that it was now not possible for them to hold power in India for longer days.

markup: Economic Policy of British
answermarkup:
1) Capitalist economy prevailed in England due to the Industrial Revolution.
2) This system was brought to India to nurture the British economy.
3) It resulted in the economic gains for England but exploitation and impoverishment of India.

markup: Audio Sources
answermarkup:
1) Recording is a form of audio source in history.
2) The discovery of technique of recording was very important.
3) Akashvani, audio tapes are considered important audio sources.
4) Jana Gana Mana sung by Rabindranath Tagore, speeches of Subash Chandra Bose, Mahatma Gandhi, speeches of leaders and personalities are broadcast from Akashvani.
5) We get to know about prevalent social, cultural, intellectual and educational history of a particular period from audio source. It is helpful for students conducting research in history.

markup: Anti Partition Movement
answermarkup:
1) With the motive to create a divide between the Hindus and the Muslims, Lord Curzon divided the province of Bengal in the Muslim-majority East Bengal and the Hindu-majority West Bengal in 1905.
2) The day of partition, 16th October was observed as the 'National Mourning Day'.
3) All over India, protest meetings were organised to condemn the decision of the government.
4) Singing of Vande Mataram and Raksha-bandhan programmes were arranged to mark the protest.
5) Government run schools and colleges were boycotted in large number by the students.
6) Sensing the intensity and severity of dissatisfaction the British annulled the Partition of Bengal.

markup: Individual Satyagraha
answermarkup:
1) As the British government was constantly neglecting the demands the Indian National Congress decided to start anti-war propaganda.
(2) Instead of a collective movement they decided every person should individually disobey the law. This is known as Individual Satyagraha.
(3) Acharya Vinoba Bhave was the first Individual Satyagrahi.
(4) After him nearly 25,000 satyagrahis participated in individual satyagraha and were imprisoned.

markup: Leadership of the struggle of 1857
answermarkup:
i. The Mughal Empire weakened during the 18th century. At this time, invaders like Nadirshah Abdali attacked India.
ii. Since, the Mughal Empire could not react to these foreign invasions; the Marathas took up the responsibility of safeguarding India and fought against Abdali at Panipat.
iii. Further, the descendant of Mughals in the freedom struggle of 1857, Bahadur Shah, was not capable of fighting against the British.
iv. Hence, Nanasaheb Peshwa, Rani Laxmibai of Jhansi and Tatya Tope took up the charge of the freedom struggle thus giving rise to Hindu-Muslim unity.
v. The revolt was led in various parts by people like Maulavi Ahmed Allah, Kunwar Singh, the Mughal commander Bakht Khan, Begum Hazrat Mahal.

markup: Reforms for women by Savitribai Phule
answermarkup:
1) Savitribai Phule, wife Mahatma Phule, advocated education along with him. of women
2) She supported her husband in his efforts to start first school for girls at Bhide Wada in Pune.
3) She continued her work in the field of education though she faced severe criticism from the society.
4) She put great efforts in women reform movement which resulted in putting an end to many unjust practices.

markup: Second Round Table Conference
answermarkup:
1) The Second Round Table Conference was held in 1931.
(2) Gandhiji participated as the sole representative of the Indian National Congress.
(3) Dr. Babasaheb Ambedkar represented the Dalits. The representatives of the various castes and communities, political parties and the princely states also participated.
(4) The issues of minority representation and nature of proposed federal constitution were discussed.
(5) Dr. Babasaheb Ambedkar demanded separate electorates for the Dalits.
(6) Gandhiji tried to bring unanimity but he was unsuccessful.
(7) So, he was disappointed and returned to India.

markup: Religious Reform Movement in Europe
answermarkup:
i. The people of Europe were ignorant and the Christian priests were taking advantage of this.
ii. The priests exploited the people in the name of religion and indulged in meaningless rituals.
iii. Hence, a movement began against it which is known as the 'Religious Reform Movement'.
iv. This movement gave more importance to human freedom and rationalism than religion.
v. During this movement, the old religious ideologies of the Roman Catholic Church were attacked by the independent intellectuals.

markup: Contribution of Dr. T. B. Kunha in the struggle for the liberation of Goa.
answermarkup:
i. Portugal denied to hand over to India, the territories under its possession including Goa.
