ii. Dr. T. B. Kunha, who was in forefront of the struggle to get these territories under India's control, worked to bring about the awakening of the people.
iii. He first established the Goa Congress Committee with the objective of building struggle against the Portuguese Government and later in 1945 founded Goa Youth League in Mumbai.
iv. Further in 1946, he violated the ban on public speech for which he was sentenced to eight years of imprisonment.

markup: Differences between Moderates and Extremists
answermarkup:
i. There were ideological differences between the Extremists & the Moderates and this difference increased in the Surat session in 1907.
ii. The resolution of Swadeshi and Boycott was being kept aside by the Moderates.
iii. The extremists tried that this opposition should not be successful.
iv. The Moderate leaders like Gopal Krishna Gokhale, Surendranath Banerjee, Pherozeshah Mehta and others blamed the Extremist leaders that they tried to capture the Indian National Congress.
v. Lala Lajpat Rai acted as a mediator.
vi. Tilak considered the Indian National Congress as a national platform and did not want it to be divided.
vii. However, during the Surat Session, tension increased a lot and since no compromise was possible, there was a split in the Indian National Congress, thus, dividing the Moderates and the Extremists.

markup: How did the British encourage English education in India?
answermarkup:
i. The British required English educated Indians for carrying out administration in India.
ii. Hence, English education started being imparted in India from 1835 on the recommendation of Lord Macaulay.
iii. Through this education, Indians were introduced to the western thoughts, modern reforms, science and technology, etc.
iv. Also, universities were established at Kolkata, Mumbai and Madras (Chennai) in 1857.
v. The western educated middle class Indian led the social reform movement in India.

markup: What were the beliefs of the Extremist leaders?
answermarkup:
i. The Extremists believed in the participation of the masses in the national movement and wanted lakhs of people to challenge the British government.
ii. They wanted the people to achieve success by struggling against the British government.
iii. They wanted to make the national movement more severe.
iv. They did not adopt the means of armed revolution but insisted for an extensive public agitation.
v. The Extremists carried forward the movement started by the Moderates.

markup: What were the social causes behind the struggle of 1857?
answermarkup:
The social causes behind the struggle of 1857 were:
1) The Indians felt that Britishers interfered in their culture, traditions and .customs.
2) The British enacted Sati Prohibition Act and the Widow-Remarriage Act.
3) These were seen as an interference in the lifestyle of the Indians.
4) Indians resented it as it was regarded as the destruction of the way of life by the British government.

markup: What reforms were introduced in the Judicial System by the British in India?
answermarkup:
1) In the pre-British period, laws were different from place to place.
2) There was difference in judgement on the basis of casteism.
3) A committee was set up to create a uniform code of law under the leadership of Lord Macaulay.
4) The Indian Penal Code was enforced all over British India with British principle of Equality before Law.

markup: What were the changes brought about by the Industrial Revolution in the system of production?
answermarkup:
1) The latter part of 18th century saw many technological innovations in Europe.
2) The production started with the help of machines running on steam.
3) The big factories replaced cottage industries.
4) Handlooms machines. were replaced by machines.
5) New modes of transport like railways and steamer were available.

markup: What were the functions of the military?
answermarkup:
1) The functions of the military were to defend the Indian territories under the control of the British.
2) It was expected to acquire new territories and quell any uprising/revolt against the British India.

markup: What were the terms of the Subsidiary Alliance introduced by Lord Wellesley?
answermarkup:
i. The Subsidiary Alliance was introduced by Lord Wellesley, after he arrived in India in the year 1798.
ii. He wanted to establish British Dominion all over India through this alliance.
iii. The alliance assured the Indian rulers of British military help, but also laid certain terms on them. They were as follows:
a. British Army was to be maintained by the Indian rulers in their court and cash or part of their territory to be paid to the company for the maintenance of this army.
b. The Indian ruler could not have any alliance or declare war on any other kingdom without the permission of the British.
c. A British resident would be stationed in the Indian ruler's state.

markup: Explain the contribution of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel in the integration of the Princely States in India.
answermarkup:
1) The problem of the merger of the princely states was very tactfully handled by Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel, the then Home Minister of India.
(2) He convinced the Princes that the merger of their states with India was in their interest.
(3) He prepared the 'Instrument of Accession', acceptable to all.
(4) The Princes accepted the proposal and all the states except Junagad, Kashmir and Hyderabad were merged with India.
(5) These three states, too, were merged with India subsequently.
(6) Thus, he took a firm stand and solved the issue of merger of princely states.

markup: What message did Dadabhai Naoroji give during the 1906 session of the Indian National Congress?
answermarkup:
i. Dadabhai Naoroji was the President of 1906 session of the Indian National Congress.
ii. In his Presidential speech, he gave the message to the people to remain united try sincerely and fulfill the aim of swaraj.
iii. According to him, this would save large number of people who were suffering from poverty, hunger, diseases and India will get a respectable position among the developed countries.

markup: Why did the Indians fail in the struggle of 1857?
answermarkup:
There are several reasons for the failure of Indians in the struggle of 1857.
They were :
1) It did not have central leadership so lacked uniformity.
2) The Indian soldiers who participated in the struggle did not have latest and sufficient weapons.
3) They were brave but did not have tactics.
4) On the other hand, the British had a unified leadership, disciplined army, latest weapons and experienced army generals.
5) The British controlled transport and communication which made their movement swift. 
6) The majority of the rulers of the Princely States kept themselves away from the freedom struggle.
7) The struggle was severe in Northern India. It did not take place all over India simultaneously.
8) Rajputana, Punjab, some parts of Bengal and North west India remained aloof.

markup: Write about the 'Kakori Conspiracy?'
answermarkup:
i. After the suspension of the Civil Disobedience Movement, many young nationalists followed the path of revolutionary activities.
ii. Revolutionaries such as Chandrashekhar Azad, Ram Prasad Bismil, Yogesh Chatterjee, Sachindra Nath Sanyal, etc. came together.
iii. They looted the government treasury that was being carried on a train on 9th  August 1925, near Kakori railway station in Uttar Pradesh. This is known as Kakori conspiracy.
iv. The government arrested these revolutionaries immediately, put into prison and were kept under trail.
v. From among these revolutionaries Ashfaqulla Khan, Ram Prasad Bismil; Roshan Singh, Rajendra Lahiri were hanged while Chandrashekhar Azad managed to escape.

markup: Which suppressive measures did the government adopt to control the anti-partition movement?
answermarkup:
The British was very disturbed looking at the influential public protest after the anti-partition movement. Hence, in order to control the anti-partition movement, the government adopted various suppressive measures. They were as follows:
i. Holding public meetings was banned and people who did not follow this were strictly punished.
ii. School children were beaten.
iii. Many restrictions were imposed on newspapers.
iv. Printing press were confiscated for criticising the government and writers & editors were imprisoned.
v. Strict action was taken against the Extremist leaders.

markup: What work did the Azad Radio Centre do during the 1942 underground movement?
answermarkup:
During the 1942 underground movement Vitthal Zaveri, Usha Mehta and her companions established a secret transmission centre, 'Azad Radio'.
The work done :
(1) News of agitations in the country were broadcast on it.
(2) Patriotic songs were sung.
(3) Patriotic speeches were telecast.
This gave inspiration to the agitators during the Quit India Movement.

markup: What resolution was passed by the Congress Working Committee on 14th  July, 1942 at Wardha?
answermarkup:
i. On 14th  July, 1942, at Wardha, the Congress Working Committee passed a resolution which demanded that the British rule in India should immediately come to an end and India should be granted freedom.
ii. The Indian National Congress also warned the British Government that if this demand was not fulfilled then India would start a non - violent struggle for acquiring freedom of India.

markup: What was Lokmanya Tilak's contribution to the national movement?
answermarkup:
Lokmanya Tilak was an Extremist leader. His contribution to the national movement is as follows 
i. Lokmanya Tilak severely criticised the suppressive policy of the British through his newspapers 'Kesari' and 'Mahratta'.
ii. The organisation of Shiv Jayanti and Ganesh Utsav was started by Tilak in order to unite the people.
iii. He stressed upon karmayog and wanted people to be always in action and for this purpose he wrote 'Gita Rahasya'.
iv. During the Lucknow session of the Indian National Congress held in 1916, Lokmanya Tilak made an attempt to resolve the dispute between the Moderates and the Extremists.

markup: What were the changes in British policy after the struggle of 1857?
answermarkup:
1) The British accepted the policy of non-interference in social and religious aspects of Indians.
2) They took care that Indian society did not unite on social grounds.
3) They took care to see that conflicts on grounds of caste, religion, race, territory kept raging.
4) They poisoned and polluted the minds of Indians by following the policy of 'Divide and Rule'.

markup: Write about the contribution of Dr. T. B. Kunha for the liberation of Goa.
answermarkup:
1) Dr. T. B. Kunha was in the forefront of the struggle to liberate Goa from the Portuguese rule.
(2) He worked to bring about awakening among the people against the Portuguese Government.
(3) With an objective of carrying out the struggle, he founded the Goa Congress Committee.
(4) He founded the Goa Youth League in Mumbai in 1945.
(5) He entered Goa in 1946 and was sentenced to eight years imprisonment for the violation of the ban on public speeches.

markup: What was the logic behind starting the non-co-operation movement?
answermarkup:
i. The logic behind starting the Non-co-operation movement was that the British government is completely dependent on the co-operation of Indians.
ii. The British government would completely collapse if the Indians adopted the policy of Non-co-operation.
iii. With this intention, Gandhiji urged the people to take part in the Non-co-operation movement and it was launched in 1920 with a resolution in the Nagpur session put forth by Chittaranjan Das.
iv. It was decided that people would boycott government offices, courts, foreign goods, government schools and colleges.

markup: State the impact of western education?
answermarkup:
1) Due to spread of western education, new ideas like Justice, Liberty, Equality, Democracy, etc. were introduced to the Indians.
2) The young Indians imbibed the values like rationalism, humanity, nationalism and scientific attitude.
3) They developed a feeling that they could carry out the work of the country.
4) English became the new medium of communication.

markup: State the provisions of the Indian Independence Act.
answermarkup:
On the basis of the Mountbatten Plan, the Indian Independence Act was passed on 18th  July, 1947.
The provisions of the Indian Independence Act were as follows:
i. Two independent nations, viz. India and Pakistan would be born on 15th  August, 1947.
ii. Once these nations become independent, British Parliament would have no control over them.
iii. The Princely States would also be free from the control of the British.
iv. The Princely States were free to join either of the nations, viz. India or Pakistan or they could remain free.

markup: Write in detail about the Brahmo Samaj?
answermarkup:
i. Brahmo Samaj was established in Bengal by Raja Rammohan Roy in 1828.
ii. He promoted the ideology of Advait philosophy after studying several languages and religions.
iii. Some of the principles of the Brahmo Samaj included monotheism, caste and class equality, protest against rituals and following the way of prayers.
iv. While it promoted widow remarriage and female education, practices like sati, child marriage, purdah system, etc. were opposed by it.

markup: What was the Montague-Chelmsford Reform Act and how did the Indians react to it?
answermarkup:
i. The Montague-Chelmsford Reform Act was passed in 1919 to bring constitutional reforms in India.
ii. This Act gave the less important departments to the Indian ministers and all the important departments like Finance, Home Affairs & Revenue were under the control of the Governor.
iii. The Indians obviously were not pleased with this Act as it did not give much exposure to the demand for responsible government in India. Tilak reacted to this Act by saying that, "This is neither Swaraj nor its foundation."
iv. The Indians realised that in order to subdue the British government to meet their demands, a more rigorous agitation was needed.

markup: Write a note on the French Revolution.
answermarkup:
i. The people of France revolted against the cruel & oppressive monarchy and feudalism in 1789AD.
ii. This revolt was known as the French Revolution and it established a Republic in France.
iii. In World history, among the political revolutions, it occupies a very important place. The world got the values of 'Liberty, Equality and Fraternity' due to the French Revolution.

markup: What was the importance of 'Azad Radio' in the underground movement of 1942?
answermarkup:
At the end of 1942, the leadership of 'People's Movement' went into the hands of young socialist activists.
i. Vitthal Zaveri, Usha Mehta and her companions established a secret transmission centre named 'Azad Radio' in Mumbai.
ii. Through this radio, patriotic songs and speeches were broadcasted.
iii. Moreover, the news of agitation also spread to various places due. to 'Azad Radio'. This encouraged the agitators.
iv. Such transmission centres were in operation for some time at Kolkata, Delhi and Pune.
Thus, the Azad Radio played a very important role in the underground movement of 1942.

markup: What changes could be seen during the Renaissance period?
answermarkup:
i. The Renaissance period saw a lot of development in the field of art, architecture, philosophy, etc.
ii. It saw the revival of Greek and Roman tradition which gave impetus to an overall development.
iii. Humanitarianism was encouraged.
iv. The outlook of the people regarding treating each other as a human being also changed.
v. Man became the centre point of all ideologies instead of religion.
vi. Moreover, the Reform movement spread throughout all sectors of human life which could be observed through science, knowledge and different sections of art.

markup: How did the conflict between Siraj-ud-Daulah and the British start?
answermarkup:
1) Siraj-ud-Daulah became the Nawab of Bengal in 1756.
2) The British traders misused trade concessions and fortified their factories in Kolkata without seeking permission from the Nawab.
3) So, Siraj-ud-Daulah captured the factory. This was the beginning of conflict between Siraj-ud-Daulah and the British.

markup: What realisation led to the emergence of a political organisation on all India level?
answermarkup:
1) English educated Indians were instrumental to bring about Renaissance.
2) They launched reform movements in social, political, religious, economic and cultural field in different parts of the country.
3) The political organisations in different parts of the country formed during various movements felt the need to create a political organisation on an all India level having common goal.
4) It was necessary to bring together groups and people who had political awareness.
5) It was necessary to draw attention of the people towards questions of the nation.
This led to the emergence of a political organization on all India level.

markup: Write about the work of Rajarshi Shahu Maharaj for abolition of caste distinction.
answermarkup:
The following work was done by Rajarshi Shahu Maharaj in his state of Kolhapur for abolition of caste distinction :
(1) He made revolutionary declaration for reservation in state of Kolhapur.
(2) There were three restrictions in the caste system : inter dining, inter marriage and change of occupation.
(3) Shahu Maharaj ate food from the hands of Dalit people and overthrew the restriction on inter dining.
(4) He passed the Act of inter caste marriage and gave it a legal acceptance in his state.
(5) He abolished 'Balutedari System' on 22 February, 1918 and granted permission to practice any occupation by anyone.

markup: Why did the British Prime Minister send Sir Stafford Cripps to India?
answermarkup:
1) During the Second World War, England sided with America against Japan.
(2) As England was ruling India, there was possibility of Japan attacking India.
(3) The Japanese forces came closer to the eastern border of India.
(4) It was necessary to have co-operation of India to resist Japanese invasion.
Therefore, the British Prime Minister, Winston Churchill sent Sir Stafford Cripps to India in March 1942.

markup: Which situations in India favoured the establishment of a political organisation at an all-India level?
answermarkup:
The situations which favoured the establishment of a political organisation at an all-India level were as follows:
i. Firstly, the newly English educated society sowed the seeds of nationalism among the people by bringing about reforms.
ii. The various movements like the Women's reform movement, the Akali Movement, etc., which took place in different parts of India created a favourable situation for the establishment of a political organisation at an all-India level.

markup: How did the British establish themselves in India?
answermarkup:
i. The European powers including the Portuguese, Dutch, French and British reached the Indian coast due to the geographical discoveries and entered the race for capturing Indian market.
ii. When the British reached India for trading, the Portuguese were already settled in India and gave a bitter resistance to the Britishers.
iii. British developed friendly relations with the Portuguese, but still had to face opposition from French, Dutch and local rulers.
In order to establish themselves in India, the Britishers had to overcome all these oppositions.

markup: Write features of Civil Disobedience Movement.
answermarkup:
The Civil Disobedience Movement launched in 1930 had the following features :
(1) All the movements launched till then were limited to urban areas.
(2) But this movement became nationwide as the people from rural areas also participated.
(3) Women participated in large numbers in the movement and even led it at many places.
(4) The movement was based on nonviolence. People faced the suppressive measures of the government unarmed and fearlessly.

markup: Which policies of Lord Dalhousie made Indians lose trust in the British?
answermarkup:
i. Lord Dalhousie annexed several princely states through various different methods.
ii. He dethroned the Nawab of Ayodhya on the grounds of maladministration.
iii. Thereafter, the princely states of Satara, Nagpur and Jhansi were annexed by him on the doctrine of lapse.
Due to these policies of Lord Dalhousie, the Indians lost trust in the British.

markup: Write about the contribution of Maharshi Vitthal Ramji Shinde.
answermarkup:
1) Maharshi Vitthal Ramji Shinde was member of Prarthana contributed in reforming society. Samaj,
2) He started the 'Depressed Class Mission'.
3) He tried to solve problems in society through this mission.
4) He organised conference against the practice of Devdasi in Mumbai.

markup: What were the main objectives of the 'Servants of India Society'?
answermarkup:
The main objectives of the 'Servants of India Society' were as follows -
i. To create love for the country among the people.
ii. To teach people sacrifice of self - interest.
iii. To destroy the differences between religion and caste.
iv. To create social harmony.
v. To spread education among the people of India.

markup: What were the consequences of struggle of 1857?
answermarkup:
1) The British government realised that there was growing dissatisfaction among the Indians due to Company's rule.
2) The British Parliament passed the Government of India Act in 1858 and took over the responsibility of ruling over people of India thus bringing an end to Company's rule.
3) The Queen issued a Declaration addressing the people of India.
4) The Governor General designated as the Viceroy of India. was
5) A new post of Secretary of State was created to look after the affairs of India.
6) The British changed the composition of army and its internal policies.

markup: Write about the work done by Mahatma Gandhi for eradication of untouchability.
answermarkup:
1) Mahatma Gandhi took up the issue of eradication of untouchability in his hands and put it up on the platform of Indian National Congress.
(2) When in Yerwada jail, he debated with rigid Hindu Pandits stating that the religious texts of the Hindus do not support untouchability.
(3) He gave inspiration to Harijan Sevak Sangh.
(4) Many took inspiration from him and dedicated themselves to the work for eradication of untouchability.

markup: Enlist the demands of the Moderate leaders.
answermarkup:
In the session of the Indian National congress, following demands were put forth by the Moderate leaders-
i. To give representation in provincial legislature.
ii. To get jobs for educated Indians.
iii. To reduce the increasing expenses of the military.
iv. To separate legislature and judiciary so that the legal rights of Indians can be protected.

markup: State the provisions of the Indian Independence Äct.
answermarkup:
1) The Indian Independence Act was passed on the basis of Mountbatten Plan on 18th  July, 1947.
According to the plan :
(1) Two Independent nations of India and Pakistan will come into existence on 15th  August, 1947.
(2) Thereafter, the British Parliament would not retain any control over them.
(3) The British supremacy over the princely states would come to an end.
(4) They would be free to join either India or Pakistan or remain independent.

markup: What brought an end to the Sikh rule in Punjab in 1849?
answermarkup:
1) After the First Anglo-Sikh War Duleep Singh remained on throne, but the power rested in the hands of the British.
2) The Sikhs could not accept the growing impact of the British over Punjab.
3) The growing influence of the British led to the revolt by Mulraj, the chieftain of Multan.
4) Thousands of participated in this war. Sikh soldiers
5) The British defeated the Sikhs in the Second Anglo-Sikh war and annexed the whole of Punjab in 1849.

markup: What inspirational message was given by Mahatma Gandhi to the people before starting the Quit India Movement?
answermarkup:
i. The Quit India Movement was to be started under the leadership of Mahatma Gandhi.
ii. He said, "Every one of you should, from this moment onwards, consider yourself a free man or woman and behave like a citizen of free India.... we shall either free India or die in the attempt.
iii. He also appealed the people to be ready to sacrifice their life with the feeling of 'Do or Die'.

markup: Why was a mixed cabinet formed after the elections of 1937 ?
answermarkup:
i. Though the Act of 1935 did not satisfy the Indian National Congress, it still decided to take part in the elections of Provincial Legislature which was provided by the Act.
ii. In 1937, elections were held in the eleven provinces of India. From among these provinces, in over eight provinces, the Indian National Congress gained majority and came to power.
iii. In the remaining three provinces, none of the parties could gain a clear majority.
Therefore, a mixed cabinet was formed after the elections of 1937.

markup: Write about Hindustan Socialist Republican Association and its objectives.
answermarkup:
i. A decision to setup a nationwide revolutionary organisation was taken by young men who were influenced by socialist ideas.
ii. They included revolutionaries like Chandrashekhar Azad, Bhagat Singh, Rajguru, Sukhdev, etc. who were secular in their thoughts.
iii. A meeting was held in 1928 at Feroz Shah Kotla ground in Delhi, where these young men established the organisation called 'Hindustan Socialist Republican Association'.
iv. The main objective of this organisation was to free India from British exploitation and also to get rid of the unjust socio economic system which exploited farmers and workers.
v. Bhagat Singh, a member of this organisation, gave importance to create a society based on social justice and equality.

markup: How did the British curtail the activities of the Hindustan Socialist Republican Army?
answermarkup:
i. After the incidence of the throwing of bombs by Bhagat Singh and Batukeshwar Dutt in the Central Legislative Assembly, the British Government immediately raided the centres of 'Hindustan Socialist Republican Army'.
ii. These raids provided the police the clues related to the killing of Saunders and they started arresting the revolutionaries.
iii. These revolutionaries were tried under the charges of sedition and on 23rd  March 1931, Bhagat Singh, Rajguru and Sukhdev were hanged in the Lahore Jail.'
iv. Although Chandrashekhar Azad did not fall in the hands of the police, he later died in a encounter with police at Alfred Park in Allahabad.

markup: How was the Indian National Army (Azad Hind Sena) formed?
answermarkup:
i. The territories in Soúth East Asia which were under the control of the British were conquered by Japan in the early part of 1942.
ii. Thousands of Indian soldiers and officers in British army were taken as prisoners by Japan.
iii. A battalion of these Indian Prisoners of war was formed by Rash Behari Bose with the help of Captain Mohan Singh. This battalion was named as the 'Indian National Army' (Azad Hind Sena) and Netaji Subhash Chandra Bose was its leader.
In this way, the Indian National Army (Azad Hind Sena) was formed by Rash Behari Bose with the help of Captain Mohan Singh.

markup: What was the condition of the women in India during the expansion of the British rule?
answermarkup:
i. The condition of women in India during the expansion of the British rule was miserable.
ii. They were not treated equal to men and were not given right to education.
iii. Also, various malpractices like child marriages, dowry system, sati, keshavapan, opposition to widow remarriage, etc. prevailed in the Indian society.

markup: State the impact of imperialistic policy of the British on India.
answermarkup:
1) The economic exploitation of India through the imperialistic policies led to the drain of the Indian wealth to England.
2) The compulsion to grow cash crops, burden of land taxes and recurring famines made conditions of farmers miserable. All these broke the backbone of the Indian agriculture.
3) With the decline of traditional industries, there was increase in unemployment.
4) The workers were exploited by the capitalists.
5) The middle class suffered due to imposition of various new taxes.
This was the impact of the British imperialist policy which led to discontent among the Indians.

markup: Why was the struggle for equality important in the making of Modern India?
answermarkup:
1) India achieved freedom because of freedom struggle.
(2) The scope of this struggle was not limited to achieve political freedom but emancipation of man from all types of bondages.
(3) Therefore in the course of this struggle, there was opposition to feudalism, social inequality and economic exploitation.
(4) The principle of equality was given equal importance.
(5) Various groups such as farmers, workers, women and dalits came forward and started movements in order to get justice and bring about reforms.
This proves that the struggle for equality has great significance in the making of Modern India.

markup: Write about the development of new industries in India during the British rule.
answermarkup:
Indian businessmen could not come forward in large numbers to start a business due to the lack of the British support. However, there were few who setup their businesses by overcoming these problems.
i. The first textile mill was started by Kawasjee Nanabhoy Davar in 1854.
ii. Similarly, the first jute mill was started at Rishra in Bengal in 1855.
iii. Jamshedji Tata started the Tata Iron and Steel company at Jamshedpur in 1907.
iv. Also, coal, metal, sugar, cement and chemical industries were started in India.

markup: How did British suppress the work of Anushilan Samiti?
answermarkup:
i. During the investigation of the incident where two English women were killed by a bomb thrown on their vehicle, the police got information about the working of the Anushilan Samiti.
ii. They arrested Aurobindo Ghosh and other members of the organisation, but were not able to prove the connection of Aurobindo Ghosh with the bombs and hence he was set free.
iii. However, other members were sentenced to long terms of imprisonment.

markup: Which events took place in the final stages of establishment of Maharashtra state?
answermarkup:
The following events took place in the final stages of establishment of Maharashtra state :
(1) Due to agitation of Samyukta Maharashtra Movement, central government gave consent to the formation of two linguistic states.
(2) The Congress President, Indira Gandhi also supported the Samyukta Maharashtra Movement.
(3) In April 1960, the Parliament passed the Mumbai Reorganisation Act.
(4) According to this act, Maharashtra State was formed on 1st  May, 1960.
(5) Pandit Nehru on the occasion of Labour Day made a formal announcement of the formation of Maharashtra State at a special ceremony at Raj Bhavan.
(6) Yashwantrao Chavan accepted the responsibility of first Chief Minister of Maharashtra.

markup: What started the demand for an independent state of Marathi speaking people?
answermarkup:
1) The demand for an independent Marathi speaking state started before independence.
(2) N. C. Kelkar presented the idea that the entire Marathi speaking population should be under one dominion.
(3) In 1915, Lokmanya Tilak demanded the reconstruction of a state based on language.
(4) An important resolution regarding Samyukta Maharashtra was passed in the Sahitya Sammelan at Belgaon. It began the movement to form Independent state of Marathi speaking people.

markup: Write about the sacrifice of Babu Genu.
answermarkup:
1) There was agitation against foreign goods in Mumbai.
(2) Babu Genu Said, a mill worker, was at the forefront in this Satyagraha.
(3) He threw himself in front of α truck carrying foreign goods in order to stop it.
(4) He did not budge even after the police threatened him.
(5) In the end, he was crushed under the truck.
(6) His martyrdom was a source of inspiration for the national movement

markup: What happened on the day a grand march was taken to Vidhan Sabha?
answermarkup:
1) For the formation of Samyukta Maharashtra, a grand march was taken to the Vidhan Sabha led by Senapati Bapat.
(2) The government declared α ban.
(3) The police started lathi charge and used tear gas on the protestors who broke the ban.
(4) On the same evening, Comrade Shripad Dange guided a mob of fifty thousand on Kamgar Maidan.
(5) To give impetus to the Samyukta Maharashtra Movement, it was further decided to hold one day strike on 21 November, 1955.

markup: Write about the attainment of independence by India.
answermarkup:
1) As per the Indian Independence Act, India was granted Independence on 15th  August, 1947.
(2) A meeting of the Constituent Assembly was going on in the hall of Parliament House in Delhi in the midnight of 14th August.
(3) At the stroke of midnight, the Union Jack of Britain was lowered and in its place the Indian tricolour flag was unfurled.

markup: What is Responsive Cooperation?
answermarkup:
1) India had to face the brunt of First World War which led to growing dissatisfaction among people.
2) To curb their dissatisfaction and get cooperation, Montague, the Secretary of State for India, declared in 1917 that Britain would gradually grant the right to self-rule and a responsible government to India.
3) Lokmanya Tilak declared that if the British Government showed sympathy and a considerate attitude to the demands of the people then the people of India would cooperate with the government. This is called 'Responsive Cooperation'.

markup: Give a brief account of the work of women social reformers for the emancipation of women.
answermarkup:
The women reformers contributed in the following way to improve the condition of women:
1) Savitribai Phule faced severe criticism of society but continued her work in the field of education.
2) Tarabai Shinde wrote the book 'Stri Purush Tulana' in which she fiercely put her views about the rights of women.
3) Pandita Ramabai founded the Sharada Sadan and took care of disabled women and children.
4) Ramabai Ranade founded the Seva Sadan Institute. She started the Nursing course for women as well as demanded the right to vote for them.

markup: What led to the discontent among the Indian soldiers in the British Army?
answermarkup:
i. The British officers gave low status to the Indian soldiers.
ii. They were not allowed to rise above the post of a Subhedar.
iii. Also, the Indian soldiers were paid less as compared to the British soldiers.
iv. Further, their allowances were also reduced gradually.
This led to a growing discontent among the Indian soldiers in the British Army.

markup: Write about the efforts taken to unite Hindu Society.
answermarkup:
1) Hindu Mahasabha was formed in 1915 to achieve respectful position of Hindu community and protect it.
2) Pandit Madan Mohan Malviya founded the 'Banaras Hindu University'.
3) Dr. Keshav Baliram Hedgewar established Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh in 1925 at Nagpur to set up a disciplinary and virtuous organisation of Hindu youth.
4) Patit Pawan Temple built by V. D. Savarkar at Ratnagiri was open to all castes of Hindu religion. He also organized common dining programmes.

markup: Give information about the work of India House.
answermarkup:
1) India House, founded by Pandit Shyamji Krishna Verma in London, was the centre of revolutionary activities outside India.
(2) It provided assistance to the revolutionaries staying abroad.
(3) It gave scholarships to the Indian students studying in England.
(4) Swatantryaveer Savarkar received such scholarship.

markup: Enlist the changes that were brought about in the administrative set up of England during the 18th- 19th century.'
answermarkup:
The changes that were brought about in the administrative set up of England during the 18th-19th century were as follows:
i. In England, there was Parliamentary Democracy. development of
ii. Changes were brought about in the structure of Cabinet System.
iii. The power of the King was limited due to the Bill of Rights, 1689.
iv. The sovereignty of Parliament was established.

markup: Why is it important to preserve sources?
answermarkup:
1) Museums, Archives preserve the sources of history.
2) This sources give evidence of our rich cultural heritage.
3) There is a great need to preserve this sources, as it is through them, that the rich tradition of history can be passed on to the next generation.

markup: How did the British crush the struggle of 1857?
answermarkup:
i. The Indian sepoys started the freedom struggle and fought it whole heartedly against the British with the help of soldiers, zamindars, kings, commanders and common people.
ii. They succeeded initially but were not able to withstand the vast military strength and the administration of British rule.
iii. The British not only crushed down the struggle by all means but also made quick recovery by regaining the lost territories within the next six months.
iv. Rani Laxmibai and Kunwar Singh and Ahmedullah lost their lives, while Emperor Bahadur Shah was imprisoned at Rangoon. Also, Nanasaheb and Begum Hazrat Mahal took shelter in Nepal. Tatya Tope who fought. for the next ten months against the British, was finally caught due to betrayal and was hanged to death.
Thus, by the end of 1858, the British ruthlessly crushed down the revolt.

markup: What were the conditions laid in Subsidiary Alliance?
answermarkup:
Lord Wellesley signed Subsidiary Alliance with many Indian rulers in 1798. Its conditions were :
1) Indian rulers should keep the British army in their Court.
2) They have to pay the company towards the maintenance of these forces in cash or a part of their territory of equivalent amount of revenue.
3) Without the intervention of the British, they would not have any alliance or declare war with any power.
4) They should keep the British resident in their court.

markup: Which constructive programmes were initiated by Mahatma Gandhi along with the non-co-operation movement?
answermarkup:
The constructive programmes initiated by Mahatma Gandhi made the national movement more comprehensive in rural areas. These programmes were as follows-
i. Spread of Swadeshi.
ii. Propagation of Hindu- Muslim unity.
iii. Prohibition of alcohol.
iv. Removal of untouchability.
v. Popularising the use of khadi.
vi. Promotion of national education.

markup: What is Industrial Revolution?
answermarkup:
i. The age of machines that began in the latter period of the 18th century in Europe, is known as the 'Industrial revolution'.
ii. This revolution first began in England and as England enjoyed industrial prosperity, it came to be known as the 'World Factory'.
iii. Industrial Revolution gradually spread to other parts of Europe.
iv. During this period, production of goods was done by machines which worked on steam.
v. Big factories replaced the cottage industries. Instead of handlooms, machines were used.
vi. Railway and steamer were used as mode of transport.

markup: Why was Swatantryaveer Savarkar sentenced to fifty years of rigorous imprisonment?
answermarkup:
i. Government got to know about the activities of Abhinav Bharat, arrested Babarao Savarkar in this connection and sentenced him to life imprisonment.
ii. A youth named Anant Laxman Kanhere killed Jackson, the Collector of Nasik, as revenge to the punishment meted out to Babarao Savarkar.
iii. Due to this, the Government started arresting all the people who were connected with Abhinav Bharat organisation.
iv. Swatantryaveer Savarkar was also linked with the murder of Jackson and was arrested and put under trial.
Thereafter, the court ordered rigorous punishment to Savarkar for fifty years.

markup: Why did the British Parliament introduce laws to keep control over the East India Company?
answermarkup:
i. In 1765, a Dual Government was introduced by Robert Clive in Bengal, wherein the revenue collection was undertaken by the East India Company and the Nawab of Bengal maintained law and order.
ii. However, money in form of taxes went into the pockets of the company officers and also the Monopoly of trade in India went to the company.
iii. Not only did other trading companies in England envy the East India Company, but the company also received strong criticism in England.
iv. Thereafter, the British Parliament introduced some important laws to keep control over the East India Company.

markup: How did India attain independence on the midnight of 14th  August, 1947 ?
answermarkup:
i. According to the Indian Independence Act, India was to be granted independence from the British rule on 15th  August, 1947.
ii. Accordingly, on the midnight of 14th  August, 1947; a meeting of the Constituent Assembly was going on in the hall of the Parliament House in Delhi.
iii. At the stroke of midnight hour, the Union Jack of Britain was lowered and it was replaced by unfurling the Indian tricolour flag.
iv. Thus, India's dependence ended and India became free from the 150 years of slavery.

markup: Write a detail description of the attack on Chittagong Armoury.
answermarkup:
1) Surya Sen drew a plan to attack the armoury at Chittagong.
(2) He and his associates raided two government armouries on the 18^"th "  April, 1930.
(3) They seized arms and ammunition from the two armouries.
(4) He took revolutionaries like Anant Singh, Ganesh Ghosh, Kalpana Datta and Pritilata Waddedar with him.
(5) They cut off the telephone and telegraph connections and succeeded in paralysing the communication.

markup: Why did Gandhiji decide to break the Salt Act to begin the Satyagraha?
answermarkup:
1) Before launching the Civil Disobedience Movement Gandhiji demanded cancellation of salt tax and end the monopoly of the British government to manufacture it.
(2) Being an important ingredient in the food of the common people, it was unjust to impose a tax on salt.
(3) Gandhiji decided to launch the Salt Satyagraha by violation of the Salt Act, which was symbolic in breaking all unjust and oppressive laws of the British.

markup: How did the various small rebellions before 1857 turned into an armed rebellion?
answermarkup:
i. Various small rebellions took place in different parts of the country before 1857.
ii. As they were local in nature, the British were able to forcibly break them down.
iii. This made the people unhappy and the discontent among diverse classes grew.
This discontent grew and blew out in form of armed rebellion of 1857.

markup: Which monuments are considered as historical monuments?
answermarkup:
The following monuments considered as historical monuments: are
1) Palaces of rulers of princely state, residences of officers, leaders and revolutionaries, forts, bridges and government offices.
2) Buildings, water supply system, fountains, roads.
3) Prisons, national monuments, etc.

markup: What useful work was done for the people by the Cabinet ministers of Indian National Congress after the 1937 elections?
answermarkup:
The useful work done for the people by the Cabinet ministers of Indian National Congress after the 1937 elections were as follows:
i. They worked towards releasing the political prisoners from jail.
ii. They introduced Basic Education.
iii. They prohibited liquor.
iv. They undertook measures to improve the condition of the Dalits.
v. They passed an Act which gave relief to the farmers from debt, etc.

markup: What were the economic causes which led to the revolt of 1857?
answermarkup:
i. In order to increase their income, the British introduced new revenue system.
ii. They forcibly extracted taxes from the farmers, which led to the collapse of the agricultural system.
iii. In accordance to their policy of selling British goods in India and enjoying the profit, the British imposed heavy taxes on the local industries.
iv. This ruined the handicraft and textile industry of India and many Indian artisans became unemployed.
These were some of the economic causes which led to a growing discontent in the minds of the Indians against the British.

markup: Write about contribution of Marathwada in the struggle for liberation of Hyderabad.
answermarkup:
The contribution of Marathwada in the liberation of Hyderabad is as follows :
(1) To secure civil and political rights of the people in the region, Maharashtra Parishad was formed.
(2) Many eminent leaders like Ved Prakash, Govind Pansare, etc. from Marathwada led the Hyderabad liberation struggle.
(3) Through 'Vande Mataram' Movement many students participated in the movement.
(4) Many sacrificed their lives in this historical struggle.
(5) The people and leaders of Marathwada had a lion's share in Hyderabad liberation struggle.

markup: Why was the struggle for independence not over in spite of India gaining independence?
answermarkup:
1) When India got independence, there were more than six hundred princely states.
(2) The French and Portuguese powers too controlled some parts of India.
(3) It was essential to merge these regions with India.
Therefore, the struggle for independence continued inspite of India gaining independence.

markup: How did the outrage of the people against the British became more severe after the partition of Bengal?
answermarkup:
i. After the partition of Bengal, more comprehensive national level movements were conducted instead of local rebellions.
ii. Youths inspired by revolutionary thoughts started establishing their secret organisations in various parts of the country.
iii. The main objectives of these revolutionaries were to have control over the British officers, to weaken the government machinery and to remove the fear of British rule from the minds of the Indians.
Thus, the outrage of the people against the British became more severe after the partition of Bengal.

markup: What were the defects in the new British system of law?
answermarkup:
i. A new code of law was introduced by the committee setup under Lord Macaulay.
ii. However, there were certain defects in this law, as there were separate courts and different laws for Europeans.
iii. Also, the new laws were difficult to understand to the common man.
iv. Apart from this, the legal cases were expensive for the community and cases remained pending for years together.

markup: What changes were seen in women due to the women's reform movement?
answermarkup:
i. Women's reform movement closed down many unjust practices in the society and broke out the voice for problems against the women.
ii. Due to this, women started putting up their own thoughts through their writings.
iii. Education also improved their performance in every sector of life.
iv. Further they also contributed a lot during the freedom struggle.

markup: Explain the objectives of Dr. Babasaheb Ambedkar in launching the Dalit movement.
answermarkup:
The objectives of Dr. Babasaheb Ambedkar in launching the Dalit movement is as follows:
(1) Dr. Babasaheb Ambedkar aimed at building a society on the principles of Liberty, Equality and Fraternity.
(2) He was of the view that unless the caste system is completely uprooted, the injustice to the Dalits and inequality would not end.
(3) According to him, social equality is the right of Dalits.
(4) He intended to carry out the movement based on self-respect.

markup: Why did the Central Government favour the making of Maharashtra?
answermarkup:
i. Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru was supposed to unveil a statue of Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj mounted on a horse, on Pratapgad on 30  November 1957.
ii. The Samyukta Maharashtra Samiti made a huge demonstration under the leadership of Bhai Madhavrao Bagal.
iii. Several other leaders like S. M. Joshi, N. G. Gore, Jayantrao Tilak, P. K. Atre, Uddhavrao Patil, etc. participated in this demonstration.
iv. Apart from this, demonstrations were also conducted at Pasarni Ghat and Poladpur.
v. These demonstrations by the Samiti succeeded in making Pandit Jawaharlal Nehru aware of the conditions and sentiments of the Marathi speaking people.
vi. Also, the Indira Gandhi, the President of the Congress party, supported the Samyukta Maharashtra movement.
Thus, the Central Government favoured the making of Maharashtra due to the agitations led by the Samyukta Maharashtra Samiti.

markup: Why did the Indian National Congress withdraw the Civil Disobedience Movement?
answermarkup:
1) After the failure of the first Round Table Conference, Prime Minister Ramsay Mac Donald hoped that Indian National Congress would participate in the Second Round Table Conference.
(2) In order to create α conducive atmosphere Gandhiji and other political leaders were released from jail.
(3) A pact was signed after discussion between Gandhiji and Viceroy Irwin.
(4) According to the pact, the British Government gave an assurance of providing Responsible Government in the proposed constitution of India.
(5) So, the congress agreed to suspend the Civil Disobedience Movement and participate in the Second Round Table Conference.

markup: How was the struggle built up by the workers decisive for the national movement?
answermarkup:
1) The beginning of the 19th  century witnessed the emergence of working class due to industrialisation. They made efforts to solve their problems.
(2) During the anti-partition movement, workers carried out strikes from time to time to pressurise the British government.
(3) The tea plantation workers in Assam launched an agitation against their wretched condition.
(4) During the anti-paritition movement, workers carried out strikes from time to time in support of Swadeshi.
(5) In 1928, the Mill Workers Union went on strike for six months. Many such strikes were organised by the Railway workers, jute mill workers, etc.

markup: Explain the events which led to the annexation of the state of Satara by Lord Dalhousie.
answermarkup:
i. Chhatrapati Pratasingh Satara was in power, even after the Peshwaship had come to an end.
ii. When Britishers signed a treaty with him, Grant Duff got appointed as an officer to assist him in the state affairs.
iii. However, soon the Chhatrapati was dethroned and sent in exile to Kashi, where he died in 1847.
iv. Later, a loyal officer of the Chhatrapati, Rango Bapuji Gupte, fought a legal battle and even went upto England. However, his efforts were unsuccessful.
v. After this, Lord Dalhousie rejected the adoption policy and annexed the state of Satara.

markup: Why are films considered effective audio-visual source of modern Indian History?
answermarkup:
1) Due to technological development there was development in photography, recording and film making.
2) Dada Saheb Phalke laid the foundation of Indian Film Industry. Many movies were made on historical events and personalities.
3) Audio-visual recordings of Dandi Yatra and on Salt Satyagraha movement are available.
4) We get information of social, political condition, dress, traditions, language of particular period from the films and audio tapes.
5) The events happened in the past could be seen in reality.
Therefore, films are considered as an effective audio-visual source of modern Indian History.

markup: State the aims and objectives of the 'Hindustan Socialist Republican Ässociation'.
answermarkup:
1) The main objective of the Hindustan Socialist Republican Association was to free India from British exploitation.
(2) It also aimed at overthrowing the unjust socio-economic order which exploited the farmers and workers.
(3) It aimed at creation of a society based on social justice and equality.

markup: Write about role of Mahatma Phule in bringing about the social reform in India.
answermarkup:
i. Mahatma Jyotirao started Phule the Satyashodhak Samaj in 1873, which worked on the principle of formation of society based on equality.
ii. The members of this samaj not only protested against untouchability but also advocated education among the depressed class and women.
iii. Mahatma Phule severely criticised the customs and traditions which discriminated between men and women.
iv. He also started the first school for girls at Bhide Wada in Pune, established the Bal Hatya Pratibandhak Gruha in his own house and also tried to eradicate the practice of keshavapan by conducting the strike of barbers.
v. He brought about the reformation of the society - through the medium of books like Brahmananche Kasab, Gulamgiri, Sarvajanik Satya Dharma and Shetkaryacha Asud.

markup: Write about the social reforms among the Sikhs?
answermarkup:
i. In order to achieve reforms in Sikh religion, the Singh Sabha was established at Amritsar.
ii. It worked for spread of education among the Sikh community.
iii. It also worked towards bringing about modernisation in the Sikh community.
iv. The tradition of reformation work among the Sikhs was further carried ahead by the Akali movement.

markup: What message did Dadabhai Nowrojee give at the session of Congress in 1906?
answermarkup:
At the session of the Indian National Congress in 1906, Dadabhai Nowrojee pronounced the word 'Swaraj' for the first time. He gave the message 
1) to remain united, 
2) try sincerely and fulfil the aim of Swaraj so that those who are poor, hungry and having diseases could be saved, 
3) India to get respectable position among the developed countries.

markup: Write about the Pitt's India Act of 1784.
answermarkup:
1) The Pitt's India Act of 1784 established a permanent Board of Control to regulate and manage administration of Company in India.
2) The Board was authorized to issue directives to the Company regarding the governance of India.

markup: State the impact of the events from 1942 to 1946 on the British rule.
answermarkup:
Many important events took place between 1942 to 1946. The following effects were seen on the British rule :
(1) It shook the foundation of British rule in India.
(2) The Quit India agitation manifested the strong anti-British feeling of the Indian people.
(3) The Army, Navy and Air Force considered to be backbone of the British power revolted against it.
(4) The British rulers realised that now their rule will not last long in India.

markup: What is Intellectual Revolution?
answermarkup:
1) Due to Renaissance, the European society stepped out of past ignorance and blind faith.
2) The pre-determined customs and traditions came to be seen from a critical point of view.
3) These changes are addressed as Intellectual Revolution.

markup: Why was the Gadar organisation setup?
answermarkup:
i. The revolutionary work against the British Government got a momentum during the First World War.
ii. The revolutionaries felt that by taking help from the enemies of the British, they can bring about the transfer of power in India. They also decided to take help of the Indian soldiers.
iii. Thereafter, various organisations were setup to take advantage of this situation, one of which was the Gadar organisation.
iv. It was established by the Indians living in America & Canada and included revolutionaries like Lala Hardayal, Bhai Parmanand, Dr. Pandurang Sadashiv Khankhoje, etc. as important leaders.

markup: Write about introduction of the English education system?
answermarkup:
1) The British were in need of Indians who had received English education in order to run the administration.
2) English education was imparted in India according to the recommendations of Lord Macaulay in 1835.
3) Indians were introduced to western thoughts, modern reíorms, science and technology.
4) They realised the need to study their history, culture, religions and also realised the drawbacks.
5) The western educated Indian middle class was responsible for initiating social reforms in later period.

markup: Why did the Indian tribes rebel against the British?
answermarkup:
i. The livelihood of the Indian tribes and forest communities was dependent on forest resources.
ii. However, the British laws put restrictions on it, which angered the Indian tribes and forest communities.
iii. Thereafter, Bihar, Kolam area of Chota Nagpur, Gonds of Orissa, Santhals of Bihar fought against the British.
iv. The British were also challenged by the Gadkaris from Kolhapur and Fond-Sawant from Konkan.

markup: Why did Lokmanya Tilak organise festivals like Shiv Jayanti and Ganesh Utsav?
answermarkup:
Lokmanya Tilak organised festivals like Shiv Jayanti and Ganesh Utsav due to the following reasons
i. Lokmanya Tilak felt that in order to strengthen the national movement, the people should forget the internal differences and come together to exchange their ideas.
ii. He also felt that common people should get inspiration from the contribution of national personalities.
iii. He was of the opinion that if people come together for religious reasons then it is not banned by the government but if people come together for political reasons then it is banned.

markup: Write about Queen's Proclamation.
answermarkup:
1) Queen Victoria of England issued a proclamation addressed to the people of India in 1858.
2) She declared that the people in India were her subjects and that discrimination would not be made on grounds of race, religion, caste and place of birth.
3) Government jobs will be given strictly on the basis of merit.
4) She promised that government will not interfere in the religious matter of the people.
5) She promised all the treaties made with the Indian rulers will be honoured and that no state would be annexed in future.

markup: Explain the philosophy of Satyagraha.
answermarkup:
1) Satyagraha, a novel technique, means insistence of truth.
2) The aim of Satyagraha was to make the unjust person aware of truth and justice and also to transform his views.
3) A Satyagrahi should never use violence and untruth means.

markup: What is 'Responsive Co-operation'?
answermarkup:
. Several factors like the war atmosphere in Europe, dissatisfaction of the Indian people and the popularity of the Home Rule Movement made it necessary for the British to seek co-operation from the Indians.
ii. Hence, the British government decided to provide some political rights to Indians and in 1917, Montague, the Secretary of State for India declared that Indians would get the right to self-government and responsible political system in phases.
iii. Tilak upon hearing this declared that if the British government shows sympathy and has a considerable attitude towards the demands of the Indians, only then the Indians would also co-operate with the British.
This policy of Tilak is known as 'Responsive Co-operation'.

markup: Which were the important provisions of the Wavell Plan?
answermarkup:
1) The Wavell Plan provided a proper representation to Muslims, Dalits and minorities in the Central and Provincial Legislatures.
(2) It provided for an equal number of Hindu and Muslim members in Viceroy's Executive Council.

markup: What kind of reaction was seen during the spread of news of arrest of main leaders of the Indian National Congress?
answermarkup:
1) Quit India Resolution moved by Pandit Jawaharlal Nehru, was passed on 8th  August with an overwhelming majority.
(2) On the same night, the leaders of the Indian National Congress were arrested.
(3) The news of these arrest aroused strong resentment.
(4) The angry people took out processions, tried to take control of government offices and attacked jails, police stations and railway stations.
(5) School children took out processions and shouted slogan "Vande Mataram".
(6) Even though the police resorted to lathi charge and firing, the people were not afraid. The young and old showed determination and courage.

markup: How were the revolts of the Indian Naval soldiers and Air Force officers an indication that the sentiments of discontent against the rulers had reached a climax?
answermarkup:
i. The Indian National Army inspired the Navy and the Air Force soldiers. They were discontented against the British Government.
ii. On 18^"th "  February 1946, the naval soldiers unfurled the tricolor flag on the British worship named 'Talwar' in Mumbai. They even raised slogans against the British Government.
iii. The British Government sent army who fired on the naval soldiers. The soldiers counter attacked them. These soldiers were supported by the workers and the common people.
iv. However, due to Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel's mediation, the naval soldiers, finally, surrendered.
v. Similarly, the officers of the Air Force from Delhi, Lahore, Karachi, Ambala, Meerut, etc., went on strike in order to extend their support to the uprising of the naval soldiers.
In this way, the revolts of the naval soldiers and Air Force Officers were an indication that the sentiments of discontent against the rulers had reached a climax.

markup: What changes came about in the field of Science, Art and Literature during Indian Renaissance?
answermarkup: The following changes were seen in the field of Science, Art and Literature during Indian Renaissance : (A) Science 1) C. V. Raman received the Nobel Prize in Science. 2) Many books were written on science which emphasized scientific outlook. 3) People realised the importance of experimentation and scientific outlook for progress of the country. (B) Art 1) Music became more popular and people-oriented. 2) A new school of painting combining traditional Indian style of painting with the western techniques emerged. (C) Literature 1) Rabindranath Tagore received the Nobel Prize in literature. 2) Stories and novels gave inspiration in gaining independence and expressed thoughts on social reforms. 3) Women took to writing. 4) New magazines and newspapers became sources of inspiration and political awakening.

markup: Write about the work Maharshi Dhondo Karve for upliftment of women.
answermarkup:
i. Maharshi Dhondo Karve started an orphanage for girls named Anath Balikashram.
ii. He intended to give education to all women and make them stand on their own feet.
iii. His efforts led to the setup of the first women's university in the 20th century.

markup: Write about the work done by Mahatma Gandhi for establishing social equality in India?
answermarkup:
i. The issue of eradication of untouchability was taken up by Mahatma Gandhi and was addressed on the platform of the Indian National Congress.
ii. When he was in the Yerwada jail, he debated with the rigid Hindu Pandits and stated that the Hindu religious texts did not support untouchability.
iii. He inspired the Harijan Sevak Sangh.
iv. He also inspired activists like Amrutlal Vitthaldas Thakkar alias Thakkar Bappa, Appasaheb Patwardhan, etc. who Keenly worked towards equality of the common people.
Thus, Mahatma Gandhi did valuable work for establishing social equality in India.

markup: Write about the various newspapers started by Dr. Babasaheb Ambedkar.
answermarkup:
The various newspapers started by Dr. Babasaheb Ambedkar are as follows:
i. He started the fortnightly 'Mooknayak' in January 1920. He handed over the control of this newspaper to his colleagues when he had to leave for higher studies to England.
ii. He also started the newspaper 'Bahishkrut Bharat' in April 1927, in which he wrote about the reformation of common people and about bringing unity among them.
iii. He also started two other newspapers, viz. 'Janata' and 'Prabuddha Bharat'.

markup: Give a brief outline of the movement in Hindu society.
answermarkup:
i. The Hindu Mahasabha was established in 1915, in order to give a respectable position to the Hindu society.
ii. Also, the Banaras Hindu University was established by Pandit Madan Mohan Malviya.
iii. Further, Keshav Baliram Hedgewar established the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangha at Nagpur in the year 1925, with an aim to set up a disciplinary and virtuous organisation of Hindu youth.
iv. The 'Patit Pawan Temple' was established in Ratnagiri for all castes of Hindu religion, by V. D Savarkar. It arranged common dinning programmes for all.

markup: Write about the work of Sane Guruji in eastern Khandesh.
answermarkup:
1) In 1938, due to heavy rains crops were destroyed in eastern Khandesh.
(2) He organised the farmers who were in miserable state.
(3) Sane Guruji organised meetings and processions at many places in eastern Khandesh to have land revenue waived for the farmers.
(4) He took out marches on the Collector office.
(5) He tried to create a strong centre of workers union at Dhule-Ammalner.

markup: Why was the Cripps Mission rejected by the political parties in India?
answermarkup:
i. In 1942, the British Prime Minister Winston Churchill had sent Sir Stafford Cripps to India.
ii. In March 1942, Sir Stafford Cripps gave the proposal of Dominion status to the Indian leaders.
iii. As there was no clear mention of complete Independence, the Indian National Congress rejected the Cripps Mission. On the other hand, the Muslim League rejected the Cripps Mission because the creation of Pakistan was not mentioned in the proposal.
Therefore, as the Cripps proposal failed to satisfy the political parties in India, they rejected the Cripps Mission.

markup: Why was the Hunter Commission appointed?
answermarkup:
1) General Dyer ordered an unrestrained firing on the unarmed people who gathered for a meeting on 13th April 1919, at Jallianwala Baug.
2) About 400 people were killed and injured. The injured did not receive any medical help.
3) There was nationwide protest against this act.
4) Rabindranath Tagore gave up the title of Sir given by the British government.
5) The Indians demanded an enquiry against this massacre.
So the British government appointed Hunter commission.

markup: Explain the contribution of Swami Ramananda Tirth in the struggle for liberation of Hyderabad.
answermarkup:
1) Hyderabad was the largest princely state in India.
(2) The autocratic ruler, Nizam had denied civil and political rights to the people.
3) In 1938, Swami Ramananda Tirth formed Hyderabad State Congress.
(4) As Nizam banned his organisation, a struggle began for getting recognition to Hyderabad State Congress and democratic rights.
5) In July, 1947 a resolution was passed by the Hyderabad State Congress for its merger with India.
6) Swami Ramananda Tirth was assisted by Narayan Reddy and Siraj-ulHasan Tirmiji in his efforts.

markup: Explain the work of Madam Cama.
answermarkup:
1) Madam Cama was related with the revolutionary work of India House.
(2) She raised the issue of India's independence at the World Socialist Conference held at Stuttgart in Germany.
(3) She unfurled the flag of India at this conference.

markup: Write about the Religious Reform Movement.
answermarkup:
1) The independent intellectuals attacked the old religious ideologies and beliefs of Roman Catholic Church.
2) The Christian priests used to give undue importance to religious rites and practices by taking advantage of the ignorance of the people.
3) They robbed people in the name of religion.
4) The movement which started against this is known Movement. as Religious Reform Movement.

markup: Why were the Sikhs defeated in the First Anglo-Sikh War?
answermarkup:
1) Ranjitsingh, the ruler of Punjab was succeeded by his minor son Duleep Singh.
2) Queen Jindan assumed the reins of administration on behalf of her minor son.
3) Taking advantage of the inability of Queen Jindan to control the officers, the British lured some of them to their side.
4) The Sikhs attacked the British under the impression that the British would invade Punjab.
5) Thus, the Sikhs were defeated in the first Anglo-Sikh war.

markup: Enlist the activities undertaken during the Non-co-operation movement.
answermarkup:
i. Eminent lawyers like Motilal Nehru, Chittaranjan Das, etc. boycotted the courts by giving up their practice.
ii. British run schools & colleges were boycotted and many national schools, colleges & universities were opened which was based on scheme of national education.
iii. The forthcoming elections were boycotted.
iv. There was boycott and bonfire of foreign clothes. This resulted in the decline in the import of foreign clothes.
v. Prince of Wales was welcomed by hartals and closed shops in 1921.

markup: State the features of the Civil Disobedience Movement.
answermarkup:
The features of the Civil Disobedience Movement were as follows-
i. Civil Disobedience Movement attracted people from all regions of the country. Not only did the people from towns and cities participate in it but also the people from villages took part in it.
For e.g. The tribal people, in large numbers participated in the Civil Disobedience Movement.
ii. There was active participation of women in this movement. Women like Kasturba Gandhi, Kamladevi Chattopadhyay, Avantikabai Gokhale, Lilavati Munshi and Hansaben Mehta led the satyagraha.
iii. Mahatma Gandhiji's principle of non-violence was completely followed in this movement. Though the British Government greatly suppressed it, the Indians fearlessly followed non-violence and protested unarmed.

markup: Write about the process of formation of Muslim League.
answermarkup:
1) The British got very disturbed by the overwhelming public response to the Indian National Congress in the anti partition movement.
2) They once again resorted to the policy of 'Divide and rule'.
3) Many British officers suggested that a separate political organisation was necessary to safeguard the interests of the Muslims.
4) Due to motivation of British government, under the leadership of Aga Khan a committee of upper class Muslims met Governor General Lord Minto.
5) Thus, encouraged by Lord Minto and other British officers, the Muslim League was formed in 1906.

markup: What was the reason behind the establishment of an all India level political organisation?
answermarkup:
The reason behind the establishment of an all-India level political organisation was as follows:
i. To bring together the various provincial political organisations.
ii. To bring together the different groups of politically aware people.
iii. To express the aspiration of the nation by diverting the attention of the people towards the questions of the nation.

markup: State the outcome of women reform movement.
answermarkup:
1) The women's reforms movement resulted in putting an end to many unjust practices in the society.
2) They voiced their problems and made efforts to find solution to them.
3) The women got opportunities to prove their capabilities in different fields.
4) Women started expressing their ideas, thoughts through writing.
5) Their performance flourished in every sphere of life due to education.

markup: Write about the Judicial system introduced by the British in India.
answermarkup:
1) The new Judicial system was introduced in India on the basis of the Judicial system in England.
2) Accordingly, each district had a Civil and Criminal Court for the respective cases.
3) High Courts were established to reconsider the judgements delivered by the District courts.

markup: Discuss the nature of reform movement related to women.
answermarkup:
1) Women had secondary position in the Indian social system.
(2) They were subjected to many injustice because of evil practices.
(3) In the 20 th century, many reforms were initiated for the betterment of women.
(4) The reform movement was led by women and institutions formed by them.
(5) They fought for issues such as right to inheritance, right to vote through medium of these institutions.
(6) The involvement of women went on increasing. They played an active role in the national movement and in the revolutionary movement.
(7) Due to the reform movement, women were included in the Provincial Ministries.

markup: What were the provisions in Regulating Act of 1773?
answermarkup:
According to Regulating Act of 1773:
1) The Governor of Bengal was designated as the Governor General. Lord Warren Hastings became the first Governor General of India.
2) It gave the Governor General controlling powers over the Bombay and Madras Presidencies.
3) It provided a committee of four members to assist the Governor General.

markup: What changes were made in administration of India after the struggle of 1857?
answermarkup:
After the struggle of 1857, the British Parliament made the following changes in the administration of India :
1) The rule of the East India Company came to an end.
2) The Governor General was designated as Viceroy of India. He was entrusted with powers to rule over people of India.
3) He carried administration under the control of British Parliament.
4) A new post called Secretary of State was created in the British Government to look after the affairs of India.

markup: How did the British capture the entire region of Punjab?
answermarkup:
i. On behalf of Duleep Singh, his mother Queen Jindan looked after the state affairs, however, she could not check the activities of the officers.
ii. The British took this as an opportunity to bribe some of the Sikh Sardars.
iii. As the Sikh Community thought that the British will attack Punjab, they attacked the British. However, in this first Anglo-Sikh War, the Sikhs were defeated.
iv. In the second Anglo-Sikh War, thousands of Sikh soldiers participated in the war but they were once again defeated.
In this way, the British, finally, captured the entire region of Punjab in 1849.

markup: Why did Gandhiji support the Khilafat movement?
answermarkup:
1) Indian Muslims started α movement to support Khalifa known as the Khilafat Movement.
2) Gandhiji felt that if Hindus and Muslims unitedly start a national movement then the government can be brought to its senses.
3) Therefore, Gandhiji supported the Khilafat movement.
4) The Khilafat committee accepted Gandhiji's proposal and extended support to the Non-co-operation movement.

markup: Why was Hutatma Smarak erected in Mumbai near Flora Fountain?
answermarkup:
i. The resolution for starting the Samyukta Maharashtra Movement was passed in the Sahitya Sammelan held at Belgaon on 12th  May 1946.
ii. The various commissions appointed by Government of India such as the Dar Commission, the Commission for the Reconstruction of States as well as the Congress appointed JVP Committee were not able to resolve the issue of formation of a state of Marathi speaking people. On the other hand, it advocated the creation of a bilingual Mumbai State.
iii. Thereafter, several leaders organised rallies and meetings as also farmers and workers along with several political parties came together and passed a resolution to create a Samyukta Maharashtra including Mumbai and Vidarbha.
iv. The discontent spread throughout the state including the rural areas and a huge public agitation aroused when it was clear that Mumbai will not be included in Maharashtra
v. Several people became martyr in the firing ordered by the State Government.
The Hutatma Smarak was erected in Mumbai near Flora Fountain in memory of 106 such martyrs.

markup: How was equality established before the law by the British?
answermarkup:
i. In India, the law differed from place to place in the early times, and different judgements were given based on castes.
ii. However, a committee was setup under Lord Macaulay to create the code of law.
iii. The India Penal Code was enforced all over the British India, in accordance with the British principle of equality before the law.
Thus, the British tried to establish equality before the law.

markup: What were the defects in the British Judicial System?
answermarkup:
The defects in the British Judicial System were as follows :
1) There were different laws and separate courts for the Europeans.
2) It was difficult for the Common people to understand the new laws.
3) It was very expensive to fight a legal case.
4) The cases got delayed and remained pending for years.

markup: What appeal did Mahatma Gandhi make in the Quit India session of Indian National Congress?
answermarkup:
Gandhiji made the following appeal to the people of India during the Quit India session of Indian National Congress at Mumbai :
(1) Everyone of you, should from this moment onwards, consider yourself a free man or woman.
(2) Everyone should behave like α citizen of free India.
(3) Either we shall free India or die in the attempt.
(4) Through the appeal he stated that Indians should be ready to make a sacrifice with the feeling of 'Do or Die'.

markup: Why was Mir Kasim made the Nawab of Bengal by the British?
answermarkup:
i. After the Battle of Plassey, 1757; Mir Jafar, the commander-in-chief of Siraj-ud-Daulah's army was appointed as the Nawab of Bengal by the British.
ii. However, when he started protesting against the British, his son-in-law, Mir Kasim was made the Nawab of Bengal and Mir Jafar was overthrown from the throne.

markup: Write about the welfare work of Chhatrapati Pratapsingh.
answermarkup:
Some of the features of the welfare work done by Chhatrapati Pratapsingh are as follows:
i. Chhatrapati Pratapsingh made provision of water to the city by building a water tank on the back side of Yevteshwar temple and Mahadara in Satara.
ii. He built roads in the city and planted trees on both sides of the road. The road built during his tenure from Satara to Mahabaleshwar to Pratapgad, further extends till Mahad.
iii. He got schools built for both boys and girls and taught Sanskrit, Marathi as well as English.
iv. He established printing press and published several useful books including Sabhaniti, a book on polity printed in 1827.

markup: Write about the military, police force and the judicial system of the British in India.
answermarkup:
i. The British military in India had the task of safeguarding the British occupied regions, acquiring new territories and also break down any revolt which may occur against the British in India.
ii. The police force on the other hand maintained law and order in the country.
iii. Apart from this, the British also established a judicial system in India based on the judicial system in England.
iv. There was a Civil as well as a Criminal court in every district to solve the local cases. In case of reconsiderations of the judgements of these courts, a High Court was established.

markup: Explain the development in the field of literature, art and science during the renaissance period in India.
answermarkup:
A lot of development took place in the fields of literature, art and science along with the social and political reform movement in India.
i. Rabindranath Tagore and C. V. Raman received the Nobel Prize in the field of literature and science respectively during this period, which led to the building of a Modern India.
ii. Also, several stories, novels and other form of writing published during this period, inspired the Indians to gain independence and also expressed thoughts on social reforms. Women also took up writing in this period.
iii. Many newspapers and magazines were also published which brought about social reform and political awakening.
iv. Art and music too developed by combining Indian styles and western techniques. A new school of paintings also came forward.
v. Several books based on science were written and people realized that for the progress of the country experimentation and scientific attitude are important.

markup: How did the British take control of the Mysore territory?
answermarkup:
i. Haider Ali took control over Mysore after a revolt.
ii. After his death, his son, Tipu Sultan, became the ruler of Mysore and he put up a tough fight against the British.
iii. Finally, in the Battle of Srirangapatna, in 1799, Tipu Sultan died.
In this way, British took control of the Mysore territory.

markup: What were the provisions in the Nagpur Pact?
answermarkup:
The following provisions were made in the Nagpur Pact :
(1) Samyukta Maharashtra should be formed including Western Maharashtra and Vidarbha along with Marathwada.
(2) Assurance was given regarding equitable financial provisions for development.
(3) Ample finance will be provided for technical and vocational education.
(4) Government services will be provided in accordance with the population in the region.
(5) Once in a year an Assembly session will be held at Nagpur.
