markup: What suppressive measures were adopted by the British government after the Second Round Table Conference?
answermarkup:
1) Gandhiji resumed the Civil Disobedience Movement after he failed and returned from the Second Round Table Conference.
(2) The government responded by resorting to inhuman oppressive measures.
(3) Civic rights were strangled.
(4) The Indian National Congress and associated institutions were declared illegal.
(4) Restrictions were imposed on national newspapers and literature.

markup: How was Simon Commission opposed in India?
answermarkup:
1) The Indian National Congress boycotted the Simon Commission because there was not a single Indian in it.
2) In 1928, when the commission arrived in India, people strongly protested against it shouting 'Simon go back'.
3) The police lathi charged the demonstrators. Lala Lajpat Rai himself led the demonstrators in Lahore.
4) He was injured in lathi charge and succumbed to his injuries.

markup: How was the Indian army reorganized after the War of Independence?
answermarkup:
After the War of Independence of 1857, the Indian army was reorganised as follows:
i. The number of British soldiers in the Indian army was increased.
ii. English officers were located at strategic locations.
iii. Important units like the artillery units were exclusively under the control of British. 
iv. In order to avoid unity of Indians to rebel against the British, the Indian Army was divided on the basis of caste.

markup: What role did Umaji Naik play in the protest against the British before 1857?
answermarkup:
i. Umaji Naik gave a strong fight to the British by organising the Ramoshis as well as the local youth for a rebellion.
ii. They were determined to overthrow the government for which they drew a declaration and appealed to the people.
iii. People of Ahmednagar, Satara, Bhor, Nasik, Pune and Solapur were inspired by the actions of Umaji Naik.
iv. Umaji Naik was arrested and hanged in Pune in 1832.

markup: What were the provisions of Morley-Minto Act?
answermarkup:
1) The Morley-Minto Act of 1909 provided for increase of the number of Indian members in the legislatures and the inclusion of some elected Indian members.
2) It created separate electorates for the Indian Muslims.

markup: What consequences were faced by the Chapekar brothers after the assassination of Commissioner Rand?
answermarkup:
i. The Chapekar brothers, Damodar and Balkrishna assassinated Commissioner Rand on 22nd  June 1897 for resorting to tyranny and force while managing the epidemic of plague in Pune.
ii. Thereafter, the British caught the three Chapekar brothers Damodar, Balkrishna and Vasudev as well as their associate Mahadev Ranade and hanged them to death.
Thus, the three brothers from the same house accepted martyrdom for the service of the country.

markup: Write about the work of Azad Gomantak Dal.
answermarkup:
i. The Azad Gomantak Dal was founded to liberate the Portuguese colonies of Dadra and Nagar Haveli in Gujarat.
ii. The youths of this group carried out an armed attack on 2nd  August 1954 and liberated the territories of Dadra and Nagar Haveli from the Portuguese rule.
iii. The important people who took part in this attack included Vishwanath Lavande, Rajabhau Wakankar, Sudhir Phadke, Nanasaheb Kajrekar, etc.

markup: Why was the Swaraj Party formed?
answermarkup:
1) The members of the Indian National Congress like Motilal Nehru and Chittaranjan Das put an idea to contest elections and enter the Legislative Assembly and Provincial Legislative Council to obstruct the working of the government and oppose the unjust policies.
2) Therefore, they formed the Swaraj Party in 1922.

markup: Why was Gandhiji sent to six years of imprisonment?
answermarkup:
1) Gandhiji was arrested in March 1922 for writing three anti-national articles in 'Young India'.
2) His trial was conducted in a special court set up in Ahmedabad.
3) The charges were levied against him. He was imprisoned for six years.

markup: Describe Subhash Chandra Bose's escape from India.
answermarkup:
i. Netaji Subhash Chandra Bose contributed greatly towards attainment of freedom for India.
ii. He gave inspirational speeches to people. Through his speeches, he appealed the Indians to revolt against the British rule.
iii. Due to this, the British government imprisoned him.
iv. In the prison, he started fast unto death. Hence, he was put under house arrest.
v. He escaped from his house after disguising himself and reached Germany in April 1941 where he founded the 'Free' 'India Centre'.
vi. From Germany, through the Berlin Radio Station, he once again appealed the Indian people to join in an armed struggle.
vii. While in Germany, he was invited to Japan by Rash Behari Bose.

markup: Write about the work of the Swaraj Party.
answermarkup:
i. The Swaraj Party was established in 1922 and in the following year, many members like Motilal Nehru, Madan Mohan Malviya, Lala Lajpat Rai & N. C. Kelkar were elected in the Central Legislative Assembly & Provincial Legislative council.
ii. Whenever the political movement in India became passive, the Swaraj Party strengthened the fight in the Legislative Assembly.
iii. They severely criticised the unjust policies of the British and demanded a Responsible Government for India in future.
iv. They made resolutions which had to be passed in the Legislative Assembly like releasing political leaders from prison, convening the Round Table Conference, etc. However, the government accepted some resolutions while rejected most of them.

markup: Explain the significance of the Quit India Movement.
answermarkup:
1) On 8th  August 1942, in the Mumbai session, the Indian National Congress gave the order of 'Quit India' to the British government. This was the beginning of a nationwide agitation.
(2) To fulfil the objective of independence, lakhs of Indians sacrificed their lives in this movement.
(3) The number of people who participated were so large that even all prisons in the country were not enough to contain them.
(4) The movement shook the foundation of British rule in India.

markup: How did knowledge and new ideas become accessible to all sections of society during the Renaissance period?
answermarkup:
i. The art and literature which was produced during the Renaissance period depicted human sentiments and emotions.
ii. For the better understanding of the people, literature was written in the local language.
iii. Moreover, the discovery of the printing press by Johannes Gutenberg helped in the spread of knowledge, new ideas and concepts to all sections of society.

markup: Write information on the workers meeting held on 7 November, 1955.
answermarkup:
1) The struggle of Marathi speaking people for formation of Maharashtra with Mumbai had started.
(2) On 7 November, 1955 a meeting of labourers was held.
(3) Labour Organisation or Communists, Praja Socialists, Socialists, Peasants and Workers Party, Janasangh, etc. participated in the meeting.
(4) Comrade Shripad Amrut Dange was the President of this meeting.
(5) S. M. Joshi proposed a resolution to create a Samyukta Maharashtra with Mumbai and Vidarbha.

markup: State the significance of French Revolution.
answermarkup:
1) The French Revolution was the first event in world history in which the might of the people's power was witnessed.
2) It had put an end to uncontrolled and unjust monarchy and the feudalism.
3) France became a Republican state. It gave the world principles of liberty, equality and fraternity.
4) The spread of democratic form of government began with the French Revolution.

markup: Enumerate the characteristics of the Presidential System of government.
answermarkup:
The following are the characteristics of the Presidential System of government :
1) The President is directly elected by the people.
2) The President has lot of powers including power to implement laws.
3) The President is not dependent on the support of the Legislature.
4) The Legislature and the Executive are not dependent on each other, but still they have mutual control over each other.

markup: State the importance of an unbiased judiciary with the help of examples.
answermarkup:
The importance of an unbiased judiciary can be observed through the following examples:
i. There can be a conflict of interest between government and an individual wherein people can approach the court for justice if a decision or law made by the government may seem unfair to the people.
ii. The objectives of social justice and equality, laid down in the Constitution, have to be implemented by the government. The judiciary supports the government through its decisions or active involvement and also by bringing the women, children, differently-abled and transgender into mainstream society.
iii. In order to strengthen democracy, it is necessary to make the common man benefit from the freedom of equality and justice which leads to widening and deepening of democracy.
iv. The Judiciary and its decisions are equal for everyone, no matter whether one is rich- poor, young- old, men or women. It thus controls the Rule of Law.
v. The judiciary protects the rights of people and all the conflicts amongst them is sorted out according to the law. This prevents emergence of repressive and authoritarian groups and individuals.

markup: What are the functions of the High Court?
answermarkup:
The functions of High Court are as follows:
i. The lower courts under the jurisdiction of the High Court are supervised and controlled by the High Court.
ii. The Fundamental Rights of citizens are protected by the High Courts.
iii. It gives advice to the Governor while appointing the judges of the District Court.

markup: Why is the legislature considered a supreme institution in a parliamentary form of government?
answermarkup:
i. The demands and aspirations of the common people are represented by the elected representatives in the Parliament.
ii. The issues of public welfare are decided by the Parliament.
iii. Also, the legislature is the House of representatives of people and expresses sovereign authority.
Due to these reasons, the legislature is considered a supreme institution in a parliamentary form of government.

markup: Why does the President seek the advice of the Supreme Court on any issue of public importance? Can you tell
answermarkup:
1) Decisions taken on issues of public importance have long-lasting effect on the lives of the people.
(2) Such decisions should also be according to the Rule of Law which treats everyone equally.
(3) Care has to be taken that such decisions should not violate the Constitution.
(4) Since the President is not a legal expert, he has to seek advice of the Supreme Court on any issues of public importance.

markup: Enlist the functions of the Prime Minister.
answermarkup:
The functions of the Prime Minister are as follows:
i. He is responsible to form the Council of Ministers and considers the administrative experience, governance skills and technical expertise while selecting the ministers.
ii. Once the Council of Ministers is decided by the Prime Minister, he allocates portfolios or departments to each minister.
iii. The Prime Minister is the leader of the Council of Ministers and presides over all the meetings.
iv. In order to maintain efficiency, the Prime Minister coordinates the working of various departments, facilitates cooperation amongst the departments as well as supervises the working of these departments.
v. Apart from these functions, the Prime Minister also is responsible for maintaining a good image of the country internationally so that the country receives a favourable opinion. He also ensures development of trust among people and provides strong support to the people who are victims of any disaster.

markup: Explain the composition of Rajya Sabha.
answermarkup:
The composition of Rajya Sabha is as follows:
1) The total membership of Rajya Sabha is 250 members.
2) Amongst them, 238 members are elected from the constituent states and Union Territories.
3) Remaining twelve members, who are distinguished personalities from the fields of literature, arts, science, sports and social work, are appointed by the President.
4) The members of Rajya Sabha are elected through the system of proportional representation

markup: Enumerate the functions of the Speaker of the Vidhan Sabha (Legislative Assembly).
answermarkup:
The Speaker is elected by the members of Vidhan Sabha. His functions are as follows :
(1) To prepare the order of daily proceedings in the House.
(2) To carry out the proceedings of the House in a disciplined manner.
(3) To suspend the members for misbehaviour or misconduct.
(4) To control and guide the proceedings of the House during sessions.

markup: Express your views on 'ideal bureaucracy'.
answermarkup:
Bureaucracy includes civil servants and all the employees working in various government offices. In India, bureaucracy is criticised most of the times and is seldom praised.
According to me, an ideal bureaucracy should function as follows :
(1) The bureaucracy should advice and force the ministers to adopt policies of public welfare.
(2) It should give full cooperation to the ministers for implementing policies effectively.
(3) It should adopt the principle of equality and an unbiased approach while implementing the policies so that maximum people are benefitted.
(4) It should make the people aware of different beneficial policies.
(5) It should strictly keep away from illpractices like corruption, unnecessary delay, cheating and frauds, etc.
(6) It should aim at establishing social justice by extending maximum benefits to weaker sections.
(7) It should function as an effective medium for development of the country, social transformation and democratisation of society.

markup: Explain how the bureaucracy provides stability to the political system.
answermarkup:
1) Bureaucracy does the work of implementing decisions taken by the ministers.
(2) Several important reforms introduced during the post-independent period have been effectively implemented by the bureaucracy.
(3) It consistently provides services like water supply, public cleanliness, transport, electricity, etc. to the people and brings stability in their day to day life.
(4) It acts as an instrument of social transformation and democratisation.
In this way, it gives stability to the political system.

markup: Do you consider Maharashtra to be progressive state?
answermarkup:
1) Industrial development has taken place in Maharashtra on a large scale. It has many industries based on modern technology.
(2) Maharashtra's literacy rate is higher than many other states.
(3) It has a rich tradition of saints and social reformers who have nurtured progressive thinking among people.
(4) Maharashtra is leading in many fields like education, health, agriculture, sports, tourism, etc.
(5) Maharashtra has been a land of Movements. Many important movements like the Labour movement, Farmer's movement have been initiated here.
(6) Similarly, many progressive laws have been passed in Maharashtra.
Maharashtra is facing many challenges like terrorism, poverty, crime, Naxalite movements, etc. Even then, I feel that Maharashtra is a progressive state.

markup: Enlist the various ways in which the Constitution can be amended.
answermarkup:
Some of the ways in which the Constitution can be amended are as follows:
i. Certain laws can be amended by simple majority of the Parliament.
ii. Some laws to be amended require of the Parliament. 2rd 3 majority
iii. Apart from these two ways certain laws are amended by special majority plus consent by more than half of the constituent states.

markup: Why does the Parliament have control over the Council of Ministers?
answermarkup:
i. The Parliament has the responsibility to ensure that the Prime Minister and the Council of Ministers functions under the Parliament and does not disregard it.
ii. In order to achieve this, Parliament exercises control over the Executive, who are drawn from the Parliament itself.
iii. Also, there are several ways in which the Parliament exercises control over the Prime Ministers and the Council of Ministers.

markup: What is a Responsible Government?
answermarkup:
1) The government system in which the Prime Minister and the Council of Ministers is responsible to the Legislature for all their actions and policies, is called a Responsible Government.
2) In this system, the Council of Ministers has to take the Legislature into confidence during governance.
3) Every decision taken by any ministry/department is considered as the decision of the government.
4) The decisions or policies of every ministry is the collective responsibility of the Council of Ministers.
5) Thus, the principle of collective responsibility adopted by the Council of Ministers makes it α responsible government.

markup: Explain the role of the Chairman of Rajya Sabha
answermarkup:
i. The Chairman of Rajya Sabha exercises control over its functioning.
ii. The Vice-President of India is the ex-officio Chairman of Rajya Sabha.
iii. The Chairman of Rajya Sabha maintains discipline in the house, facilitates discussions, ensures that the members get a chance to speak, etc.

markup: Mention the functions of the High Court.
answermarkup:
The functions of the High Court are as follows:
(1) To supervise over the District and other lower courts in its jurisdiction.
(2) To maintain control over the functioning of the lower courts.
(3) To give orders to protect the fundamental rights of the citizens.
(4) To give advice to the governor while appointing judges in the district courts.

markup: Write about Lok Sabha elections.
answermarkup:
1) Since Lok Sabha is a House of people's representatives, elections are held after every five years.
2) Elections to Lok Sabha which are held every five years are known as General elections.
3) When Lok Sabha is dissolved before the completion of five years and elections are held, such elections are called mid-term elections.
4) When a member resigns or dies suddenly, election held for such a seat is called by-election.

markup: What kind of heads are the President and the Prime Minister and what kind of relationship exists between the both?
answermarkup:
i. President is a nominal head where as the Prime Minister is the executive head.
ii. The Government is actually run by the Prime Minister and the Council of Ministers, though it is run in the name of the President.
iii. The conduct of the administration is informed to the President regularly by the Prime Minister by meeting him regularly.
iv. The Prime Minister also informs the President about new laws and policies.
v. The President has a right to seek any information from the Prime Minister.

markup: Which are the provisions that preserve the independence of the judiciary?
answermarkup:
The Constitution has made following provisions to preserve the independence of the judiciary :
(1) To avoid any political pressure, judges are appointed by the President.
(2) Judges enjoy the security of tenure. They cannot be removed from the post for trivial reasons or for political motives.
(3) The salaries of the judges are drawn from the Consolidated Fund of India. No discussion regarding this takes place in the Parliament.
(4) Personal criticism cannot be made on judges for their acts and decisions. It is considered as contempt of court and is a punishable offence.
(5) The Parliament cannot discuss the decisions of the judges.

markup: Write in short about the British Parliament?
answermarkup:
i. The Parliamentary system of government developed in England.
ii. The governance of the country is carried out in accordance with the traditions, customs and conventions.
iii. The British Parliament has evolved over a period of time.
iv. Thus, it can be said that, the Parliamentary system of government has its roots in the 'Parliament'.

markup: What are the key features of the Lok Sabha?
answermarkup:
The key features of the Lok Sabha are as follows:
i. The members of the Lok Sabha are directly elected by the people.
ii. Lok Sabha has fixed number of people.
iii. Elections to the Lok Sabha are held at regular intervals.
iv. These elections are contested by all the major political parties.

markup: How is equal representation to all sections of the community ensured in the Lok Sabha?
answermarkup:
i. Lok Sabha is the representative body of the citizens of the country.
ii. There can be a maximum of 552 members in a Lok Sabha as per the constitution, which should ensure representation of all sections of the community.
iii. In order to achieve this, some seats in the Lok Sabha are reserved for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes.
iv. Also, President can nominate two members from Anglo-Indian community to the Lok Sabha, if there are no representatives from this community.

markup: Mention the eligibility conditions for contesting Vidhan Sabha elections.
answermarkup:
Following are the eligibility conditions for candidates contesting for Vidhan Sabha elections :
(1) He/ She should be a citizen of India.
(2) He/  She should have completed 25 years of age.
(3) He/  She should be a resident of Maharashtra.

markup: How does the Parliament keep a check on the Executive?
answermarkup:
The Parliament keeps a check on the Executive in the following ways:
1) The bills/proposals presented by the Council of Ministers are discussed in the Parliament.
2) These discussions and debates help the members to scrutinise the bills/proposals and point out the short comings, and help in creation of healthy laws.
3) During Parliamentary sessions, the proceedings of the House begins with questions asked by the members of the House. The concerned Ministers are expected to give satisfactory answers to these questions.
4) During the Parliamentary sessions, the period around 12 noon is called as 'Zero House'. During this period, any question of public importance can be raised and discussed.
5) The Parliament can pass a No-confidence motion on the Executive. If the motion is passed with majority support, then it has to resign.

markup: Explain the functions of the Speaker of Lok Sabha.
answermarkup:
The functions of the Speaker of Lok Sabha are:
1) To conduct the business of the House in an unbiased manner.
2) To take care of the rights and privileges of the members of Lok Sabha.
3) To interpret the rules of daily functioning of the House and work accordingly.
4) To maintain the decorum and dignity of the House.

markup: Why did the Constitution adopt a federal system for India?
answermarkup:
1) India is a country having large geographic expanse.
(2) It has a multicultural population.
(3) There is a great diversity in language, religion, ways of life and regional characteristics.
(4) It would not have been possible to govern such a huge country from a centralised place.

markup: State the qualifications necessary for contesting the Presidential election.
answermarkup:
1) The person contesting the Presidential election should be a citizen of India.
2) He should be 35 years of age.
3) He should also fulfill other conditions mentioned by the Constitution.

markup: How is the President of India elected?
answermarkup:
i. The President of India is elected indirectly by the people of India.
ii. It means that the common people are not able to vote in the election of the President.
iii. The directly elected representatives that include the members of the Central and State legislatures vote and elect the President.
iv. These members of the parliament and that of the state legislatures are together known as the Electoral College.

markup: In India we have Prime Minister but why is there no Prime Minister in the United States of America?
answermarkup:
1) In the Parliamentary System of government, the Prime Minister is the head of the Executive, i.e. the Council of Ministers.
2) In the Presidential System of government, the President is the head of the Executive.
3) Since India has adopted the Parliamentary system, we have the post of the Prime Minister.
4) Since United States of America has adopted Presidential System, they have the post of the President.
5) The post of the Prime Minister does not exist in Presidential System of government.

markup: Explain the characteristics of Bureaucracy.
answermarkup:
1) Bureaucracy is the administrative system which actually implements the government's policies.
(2) Though the government changes, bureaucracy remains constant. Thus, it is permanent in nature.
(3) It has to remain politically neutral and discharge its duties.
(4) Its anonymity is maintained, i.e. it is not held directly responsible for any success or failure of policies and it is never publicly criticized.
Thus, the structure of Bureaucracy in India is extensive and complex.

markup:
What are the considerations of the Chief Minister while allocation of portfolios? 
                               OR
Formation of Council of Ministers is a challenging task for the Chief Minister.
answermarkup:
After the formation of the Council of Ministers, the Chief Minister has to distribute portfolios among the ministers. He has to consider following aspects -
(1) Some portfolios are of prime importance while others are of secondary importance. He has to select appropriate people for each portfolio.
(2) He has to consider the experience and the efficiency of the ministers he has selected.
(3) The political experience and administrative skills of the concerned ministers is also taken into consideration by him.
(4) Other factors like the awareness of public issues, effective leadership, etc. are also considered by him.
(5) If the government is in coalition, he has to distribute portfolios appropriately among the constituent parties in the alliance.

markup: What is a Parliamentary System of government?
answermarkup:
1) The Parliamentary System of government is the one where representatives are directly elected by the people.
2) They are the members of the Legislature, which is also known as the Parliament.
3) In this system, elections are held after fixed period.
4) The party which gets the majority forms the government.
5) In this system, the Executive is dependent on the confidence of the Legislature.

markup: How are members of the Lok Sabha elected?
answermarkup:
1) As per the Constitution, there can be a maximum of 552 members in Lok Sabha.
2) General elections to Lok Sabha are held after every five years and members are directly elected by the people.
3) To ensure equal representation to all sections of the community, some seats are reserved for members belonging to Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes.
4) In case there are no representation from the Anglo-Indian community, the President can appoint two members from this community to the Lok Sabha.
5) Thus, Lok Sabha is the representative body of the citizens of India.

markup: Write about the formulation of laws by the Parliament.
answermarkup:
i. New laws are formulated by the Parliament to achieve the welfare of the people and the objectives of the Constitution.
ii. While changes are made in certain laws and some outdated laws are repealed.
iii. The process of making laws by the Parliament has been described in the Constitution.

markup: What is the significance of Indian bureaucracy?
answermarkup:
i. The Indian bureaucracy has an extensive and complex structure.
ii. It has effectively implemented several important reforms which were introduced in the postindependence period.
iii. Also, many positive changes are seen due to the implementation of the Government policies by the Indian bureaucracy.
iv. It brings stability to the political system as well as to the people by ensuring provision of their daily needs like water supply, cleanliness, health, agricultural reforms, prevention of pollution, etc.
v. It also ensures implementation of policies and laws enacted by the government for women empowerment, child security, plans for marginalised sections, etc. Thus, Indian bureaucracy becomes an important instrument of social transformation.
vi. Also, Indian bureaucracy plays an important role in the democratisation of the society by bringing marginalised sections in to the main stream through reservation policy.

markup: What is the role of the executive in a parliamentary system of government?
answermarkup:
i. In a parliamentary form of government the executive, comprising of the Prime Minister and the Council of Ministers has responsibility. a dual
ii. Laws are implemented by them since they are the executive.
iii. They also have to fulfill responsibilities of the legislature since they are members of the legislature.

markup: Enumerate the functions of the Council of Ministers.
answermarkup:
The functions of the Council of Ministers are as follows:
1) The Council of Ministers takes initiative in the process of Law-making by drafting the bills/proposals.
2) It introduces and discusses the bills/proposals in the House.
3) It introduces bills on various subjects like education, agriculture, industry, health, foreign relations, etc. in the Parliament, conducts discussions on them and tries to get them approved by the Parliament.
4) It also takes the responsibility of implementing the policies approved by the Parliament.

markup: Explain the role of bureaucracy in the democratisation of society.
answermarkup:
1) Equality and social justice are important values of democracy.
(2) Bureaucracy has helped in bringing marginalised sections of society into the
mainstream by implementing the reservation policy effectively.
(3) Their participation has been increased in the process of decisionmaking.
(4) Democratisation of society not only requires progressive laws and policies but also effective participation of bureaucracy in implementing it.
Thus, bureaucracy plays an important role in the democratisation of society.

markup: Which are the two fundamental types of functions performed by the government of any country?
answermarkup:
The two fundamental types of functions performed by the government of any country are:
i. Defending the country from external aggression and internal threats.
ii. Providing various services to citizens so as to ease their daily lives and enable them to develop themselves as well as the society.

markup: Why are laws necessary in society?
answermarkup:
1) Differences in opinions, thoughts, perspectives, different cultures of people give rise to conflicts. These conflicts can be resolved impartially by the Judiciary.
(2) Social justice and equality in society can be established with the help of law.
(3) It also helps to bring weaker sections of the society, women, children differentlyabled and transgenders into the mainstream of the society.
(4) Law helps the common man to get the benefits of values of freedom, equality and democracy.
(5) Law helps to protect the rights of the people.
(6) It prevents emergence of repressive and authoritarian groups and individuals.
Hence, laws are necessary in society.

markup: How is the Council of Ministers formed?
answermarkup:
1) The party which attains majority in the Lok Sabha election, nominates its leader as the Prime Minister.
2) The Prime Minister is given an oath by the President.
3) The Prime Minister then, chooses his trustworthy and efficient colleagues from within the party to form the Council of Ministers.
4) He gives priority to his colleagues considering their administrative experience, governance skills, efficiency and technical expertise.
5) The President administers oath to all the Council of Ministers.
In this way, the Council of Ministers is formed.

markup: Mention the ways of amending the Constitution.
answermarkup:
The Constitution can be amended in following ways:
1) Few provisions in the Indian Constitution can be amended by simple majority.
2) Some provisions require special (2/3rd) majority of the Parliament.
3) Few other provisions can be amended by special majority plus consent from more than half of the constituent states.

markup: How does the government carry out the function of providing security for the country?
answermarkup:
i. The government protects the country from external aggression and internal threats.
ii. The security of the country is carried out by the armed forces.
iii. The internal security is also maintained as aid to civil authority:
In this way, the government carries out the function of providing security for the country.

markup: Explain the role of the ministers and civil servants in the efficient administration of the department.
answermarkup:
1) The efficiency of a particular department depends upon the interrelationship between the Minister and his Secretary and Deputy secretary.
(2) The decisions taken by the Ministers are based on the necessary information provided by the bureaucracy.
(3) The bureaucracy, i.e. civil servants have complete information about the financial provisions for a particular scheme or plan and also about the history of successes and failures of policies.
(4) Hence, if the Ministers develop mutual trust and transparency with the civil servants, it will help in the efficient administration of the department.

markup: What is the difference between a Parliamentary and a Presidential System of government?
answermarkup:
Difference between the Parliamentary and Presidential System of government is as follows:
Parliamentary System Presidential System
1) President is the Constitutional Head. President is the Executive Head.
2) Prime Minister and Council of Ministers have more powers. President has more powers.
3) Council of Ministers is formed by the elected members of Parliament. President is directly elected by the people.
4) Parliament can remove the Prime Minister by passing a no-confidence motion. President can be removed only by impeachment.
5) Members of the Executive are also the members of the Legislature. Legislature and Executive are not dependent on each other.

markup: Should the Supreme Court have the power of Judicial Review?
answermarkup:
The Supreme Court must have the power of Judicial Review for following reasons :
(1) Protecting the Constitution is the most important responsibility of the Supreme Court.
(2) Many a times, laws violating the Constitution are passed under public pressure or for gaining popularity.
(3) The Executive may pass laws or frame policies violating the Constitution.
(4) Laws violating the fundamental rights of the citizens may be passed which may prove to be harmful for democracy.
(5) The power of Judicial Review helps in curbing all anti-constitutional practices and protects and strengthens democracy.
(6) It also helps in keeping the Executive under control.

markup: Explain the functions of the Parliament.
answermarkup:
In order to achieve welfare of the people and the objectives of the Constitution, the Parliament has to perform following functions:
1) To formulate new laws and to repeal the outdated laws.
2) To make necessary changes in the existing laws.
3) To amend the Constitution wherever necessary.
4) To keep control over Council of Ministers.

markup: What are the eligibility criteria for appointment of Supreme Court judges?
answermarkup:
The eligibility criteria laid down by the Constitution for appointment of Supreme Court judges are as follows:
(1) He/She must be a citizen of India.
(2) He/ She must be a legal expert.
(3) He/She must have served as a High Court judge or as an experienced advocate in the High Court.

markup: Enumerate the functions of the Supreme Court.
answermarkup:
The functions of the Supreme Court are as follows :
(1) As a federal court, it has the responsibility to settle disputes between the centre and the states; and states on one side and states on the other.
(2) It gives orders to relevant authorities to protect the fundamental rights of the people.
(3) It has the power to review decrees and orders of the lower courts and also review its own decisions.
(4) It provides necessary advice to the President if he/she asks for advice to understand the legal aspects in matters of public importance.

markup: How is democratisation of society achieved?
answermarkup:
The democratisation of society is achieved in the following ways:
i. The reservation policy helps in bringing the marginalised sections of society into the mainstream.
ii. The bureaucracy ensures increased participation of this section in the decision making process.
iii. Thus, democratisation of society not only requires progressive laws but also the effective participation of bureaucracy.

markup: Explain the steps involved in the law making process.
answermarkup: The Bill undergoes following process in order to be converted into a Law (Act). 1) First reading i) The minister of the concerned department/ministry or member of the Parliament presents the bill in the House. ii) The objectives and the structure of the Bill are mentioned. (2) Second reading i) The positive and negative points of the bill are discussed. ii) The defects and faults in the bill are stressed. iii) After removing the defects and the faults, the bill is put to vote. (3) Committee Stage i) Sometimes, if required, the Bill is sent to the committee of the House. ii) The Bill is discussed in the Committee in details. iii) The Committee report consisting of instructions and recommendations is sent to the House. iv) The Bill is discussed clause by clause and then voting is taken. (4) Third reading i) The Bill is once again discussed in the House. ii) Voting is taken for approving the Bill. (5) Approval of the other House i) The Bill has to undergo the same procedure even in the other House. ii) The Bill is approved by majority. (6) Assent by the President i) After getting an approval from both the Houses, the Bill is further sent for assent by the President. ii) After the final assent and signature of the President, the Bill is converted into Law.

markup: What is the job of the Members of Parliament?
answermarkup:
i. The members of the Lok Sabha and the Rajya Sabha are together known as the Members of the Parliament (MPs).
ii. They raise questions in the Parliament and try to resolve the queries and complaints of their constituencies.
iii. They are allocated funds by the government, which they use to carry out development activities in their constituencies.

markup: Mention the functions of the Prime Minister.
answermarkup:
The functions of the Prime Minister are as follows:
1) To form the Council of Ministers, selecting trustworthy, experienced and efficient people.
2) To allocate portfolios and chair all the meetings of the Council of Ministers.
3) To lead the Council of Ministers, maintain coordination among various departments, facilitate cooperation among departments and supervise to bring about efficiency and efficacy.
4) To raise the image of the country at international level.
5) To support the people during disasters.

markup: How is the President elected?
answermarkup:
1) The President is not directly elected by the people of India.
2) The common people do not vote in the election of the President.
3) He is elected by the Electoral College.
4) The Electoral College includes all members/elected representatives of Parliament and the members of the State Legislatures.

markup: Explain the composition of the Rajya Sabha.
answermarkup:
i. There are in all 250 members in the Rajya Sabha. These members are elected through the system of proportional representation out of the total population of the electorate.
ii. Out of the total members, 238 members are elected from the States and Union Territories of the country.
iii. Remaining 12 members are appointed by the President.
iv. These members are generally distinguished personalities from the field of arts, literature, science, sport and social work.

markup: Why have autonomous institutions like Public Service Commissions been established?
answermarkup:
The Constitution of India has established autonomous institutions like Public Service Commissions for following reasons :
(1) To select civil servants.
(2) To conduct competitive exams for selecting candidates on the criteria of merit and efficiency.
(3) To decide other aspect to like the nature of the exam, syllabus, eligibility, etc.
(4) To select efficient and deserving candidates through interviews and recommend them to the government for appointment.

markup: Explain the significance of Indian bureaucracy.
answermarkup:
1) The Indian bureaucracy implements the policies made by the government for the welfare of the people effectively.
(2) It provides several essential services to the people consistently and brings stability in their day to day life.
(3) It provides stability to the political system.
(4) It acts as an important instrument of social transformation and democratization of society.

markup: We should preserve historical monuments.
answermarkup:
1) Monuments are witness to our glorious past. Many monuments are connected to freedom fighters and their work.
2) Sevagram Ashram at Wardha and Mani Bhavan at Mumbai give information about the Gandhian era. us
3) The cellular jail at Andaman is a witness to the sufferings of V. D. Savarkar and his revolutionary work.
4) We get information about contemporary history, architecture, nature of monument and the economic condition of that particular period.
5) We get to know our history because of monuments and they invoke nationalistic feeling among us.

markup: Gandhiji withdrew the Civil Disobedience Movement in April 1934.
answermarkup:
i. Gandhiji returned India disappointed from the Second Round Table Conference held at London in 1931.
ii. He then decided to relaunch the Civil Disobedience Movement in 1932. The British Government immediately arrested Gandhiji which led to discontent among the Indians.
iii. The Government used inhuman oppressive methods in order to suppress the movement.
iv. The civil rights were curtailed everywhere. Restrictions were imposed on newspapers and literature. Moreover, the Government declared the Indian National Congress and its associated institutions as illegal.
Therefore, Gandhiji withdrew the Civil Disobedience Movement in April 1934 and the second phase of the movement also ended.

markup: Severe response was seen throughout Maharashtra against JVP Committee report.
answermarkup:
1) The Congress appointed a three ministers committee on 29 December, 1948 to study the conditions of creating linguistic provinces.
(2) The report suggested that Congress accepted the concept of linguistic state in principle but the time was not proper for it.
(3) Due to this, severe response of the people was seen throughout Maharashtra against JVP Committee report.

markup: Dr. Babasaheb Ambedkar started newspapers like 'Muknayak', 'Bahishkrut Bharat', etc.
answermarkup:
1) Dr. Babasaheb Ambedkar wanted to establish a society based on principles of Liberty, Equality and Fraternity.
(2) He intended to carry out movement to establish self-respect and social equality for Dalits.
(3) It was necessary to create awakening in society in this respect and to voice their grief.
(4) The newspaper was an integral part of Dr. Babasaheb Ambedkar's movement.
(5) Hence, he started many newspapers so that his ideas and thoughts reach the society.

markup: Salary of company officers were increased.
answermarkup:
1) Lord Cornwallis introduced bureaucracy in India to strengthen the British rule in India.
2) He restricted the private trade carried out by the company officers.
For this reason, he increased the salary of the company officers.

markup: The Paikas made armed rebellion against the British.
answermarkup:

3) The life of the common man became miserable due to tax imposed on salt by the British.
This resulted in armed rebellion of the Paikas against the British in 1817.

markup: Khilafat movement was started in India.
answermarkup:
1) The ruler of Turkey was regarded as the Khalifa or religious head of the Muslims all over the world.
2) To get the support of Indian Muslims, in the First World War, the British gave false assurance of not harming the Khalifa's empire after the war.
3) But they did not keep their word. It caused resentment among the Indian Muslims.
So, they started the Khilafat Movement.

markup: There was discontent among the Indian soldiers.
answermarkup:
1) Indian soldiers were treated with contempt.
2) They were denied position higher than Subhedar in the army.
3) They were given low status by the British officers.
4) They were paid less salary than the British soldiers.
5) Their allowances were reduced gradually.
Due to all these factors there was discontent among the Indian soldiers.

markup: The British Parliament introduced some laws to keep control over the affairs of the company.
answermarkup:
1) The 'Dual Government' system was introduced by Robert Clive in Bengal in 1765.
2) But, sometimes, the officers of the company pocketed money.
3) As monopoly of trade was given to East India Company, many trading companies in England envied them.
4) The working system of the company was criticised in the British Parliament.
So, to keep control on the affairs of the company, the British Parliament introduced some laws.

markup: Gandhiji was arrested on 4th  May 1930.
answermarkup:
1) Gandhiji started Salt Satyagraha on 6th  April 1930 at Dandi by breaking the Salt act.
(2) With this the Civil Disobedience Movement started all over India.
(3) In spite of suppressive measures undertaken by the British Government, they could not suppress the movement. The British government found itself in difficult situation.
So, Gandhiji was arrested on 4th  May 1930.

markup: Swatantryaveer Savarkar was sentenced to fifty years of rigorous imprisonment.
answermarkup:
1) On knowing the activities of Abhinav Bharat, the government arrested Babarao Savarkar and sentenced to life imprisonment.
(2) Anant Laxman Kanhere killed Jackson, collector of Nashik in retaliation.
(3) The government linked Abhinav Bharat and Savarkar with his murder.
(4) He was arrested and put on trial. So, the court sentenced him to fifty years of rigorous imprisonment.

markup: Britishers entered into Maratha politics.
answermarkup:
1) Marathas had a strong hold on the areas in and around Mumbai which was prime centre of British in western India.
2) British tried to acquire nearby territories but the Marathas checked their expansion.
3) It was only after the death of Peshwa Madhavrao, that they got entry in Maratha politics. Raghunathrao in his greed for Peshwaship sought their help.
This led to the entry of the British in Maratha politics.

markup: Dr. Babasaheb Ambedkar started a Satyagraha at Chavdar Lake in Mahad.
answermarkup:
Babasaheb Ambedkar started a Satyagraha at Chavdar Lake in Mahad because-
i. Babasaheb Bole got a Bill passed in the Bombay Provincial Assembly which granted the untouchables the use of public water reservoirs.
ii. However, the Dalits were not allowed to use of these water reservoirs.
Therefore, Dr. Babasaheb Ambedkar started a Satyagraha at Chavdar Lake in Mahad.

markup: The period between 18th and 19th century came to be known as 'Age of Revolutions'.
answermarkup:
1) The British Parliament passed The Bill of Rights in 1689. It established sovereignty of Parliament and curtailed powers of the King.
2) This gave momentum to the development of Parliamentary Democracy in England.
3) The thirteen British colonies in America won the War of Independence in 1783.
4) These thirteen colonies established the first federal republic, known as the United States of America.
5) The people of France revolted against the unjust and uncontrolled monarchy and feudalism. They established a Republic.
6) The industrial revolution in Europe in the latter part of the 18th century brought revolutionary changes in Europe.
7) These changes had long lasting effect on the entire world.
8) All these revolutionary events took place during 18th and 19th century period.
Hence it is known as the 'Age of Revolutions'.

markup: The British captured Sindh in 1843.
answermarkup:
i. The British turned their attention towards the north-west frontier in order to strengthen their position in India.
ii. They were cautious about Russia and were worried that it might attack India through Afghanistan. Hence, the British felt the need to establish their influence in Afghanistan.
iii. Since the route towards Afghanistan went through Sindh, British understood the importance of Sindh.
Therefore, the British captured Sindh in 1843.

markup: The British government passed the Rowlatt Act in 1919.
answermarkup:
1) Indians extended help to the British government in the First World War.
2) The Indians expected that after the war is over there will be a system of governance for taking decision for the well-being of the Indians.
3) Moreover, the rising prices, increased taxes led to growing unrest among the Indians.
4) To suppress this discontent and suggest measures about it Rowlatt Act was passed in 1919.

markup: England was described as 'World Factory.'
answermarkup:
1) There were many revolutionary changes in the latter part of the 18th century in Europe.
2) Many technological innovations in Europe gave enormous outputs.
3) Goods were produced with the help of machines running on steam and later on electricity. It was the dawn of the age of machines.
4) Though the industrial revolution started in England it gradually spread to other parts of the western world.
5) During this period, England enjoyed industrial prosperity and was described as World Factory.

markup: Gandhiji began fast unto death in the Yerwada jail.
answermarkup:
1) The Communal Award declared by the British Prime Minister Ramsay Mac Donald provided separate electorates for the Dalits.
(2) This division of the society on the basis of caste was not acceptable to Gandhiji.
(3) Therefore, to protest against the Award, Gandhiji began fast unto death in the Yerawada jail.

markup: European rulers started giving military protection and trade concessions to the trading companies.
answermarkup:
1) With the discovery of new sea routes to the east, trade with oriental untries became very profitable. Thus, the European trade prospered.
2) Competition for trade began among many European nations.
3) The traders pooled their resources and formed trading companies like the East India Company.
4) As this trade brought economic prosperity, the European rulers started giving military protection and trade concessions to these trading companies.

markup: Narayan Meghaji Lokhande is described as 'Father of Indian Workers Movement'.
answermarkup:
1) Industrialisation of India had started during the second half of the 19th century.
(2) Shashipad Banerjee and Narayan Meghaji Lokhande organised workers at local level and made efforts to solve their problems.
(3) Narayan Meghaji Lokhande formed the mill workers union known as 'Bombay Mill Hands Association' in 1890.
(4) Due to his efforts, the workers started getting weekly holiday on Sunday from 10 June, 1890.
(5) This was the beginning of organised movement in India.
Thus, his contribution to the working class movement was so valuable that he is described as 'Father of Indian Workers Movement'.

markup: The working of Interim Government could not run smoothly.
answermarkup:
1) Muslim League demanded separate Muslim nation of Pakistan.
(2) The followers of the Muslim League resorted to violent ways.
(3) Though the Muslim League declined to participate initially, they later participated in it.
(4) However, the leaders of the Muslim League adopted the policy of obstruction and therefore the Interim Government could not run smoothly.

markup: The European countries felt the necessity of finding new sea routes to Asia.
answermarkup:
1) The Ottoman Turks captured Constantinople, the capital of Byzantine Empire, in 1453 AD.
2) All land trade routes joining Asia and Europe passed through this city.
3) It stopped the flow of valuable goods from the countries in the east.
Therefore, the European countries felt the necessity of finding new sea routes to Asia.

markup: The Cabinet Mission Plan could not satisfy the political parties in India.
answermarkup:
The Cabinet Mission Plan could not satisfy the political parties in India because,
(1) The Indian National Congress was not happy with some of its provisions.
(2) The Muslim League was also dissatisfied with the plan as it did not provide for the creation of a separate Muslim state of Pakistan.

markup: The role of newspapers was important in Samyukta Maharashtra Movement.
answermarkup:
1) The role of newspapers was equally important in Samyukta Maharashtra Movement. They worked to awaken the people.
(2) Navyug, Prabhat, Navakal, Sakal, Prabodhan, Kesari are newspapers which played important role.
(3) The 'Maratha' newspaper by Acharya Atre had a significant role in Samyukta Maharashtra movement.
(4) Balasaheb Thackeray took pen name 'Mavla' and drew caricatures in 'Navyug'.
(5) Lokshahir Annabhau Sathe, Shahir Amar Sheikh and Shahir D. N. Gavankar
aroused public awakening on a large scale through their writings.

markup: The Cabinet Mission was not fully accepted by the Indian National Congress and the Muslim League.
answermarkup:
i. Following the end of the Second World War, the British rulers decided to give freedom to India. Hence, in the Parliament, the British policy regarding India was clarified by the British Prime Minister Attlee.
ii. Accordingly, the Parliament recognised the right of the Indian people to draft their own Constitution. It also declared that the issue of minorities will not become an obstacle while granting freedom to India.
iii. In March 1946, England's plan regarding India was explained to the Indian leaders by representative of British ministers, viz., Pethick Lawrence, Stafford Cripps and A. V. Alexander. This was known as the 'Cabinet Mission'.
iv. Some provisions of this plan were not liked by the congress. Similarly, the Muslim League was not satisfied since the provision for the creation of a separate independent state for the Muslims was not mentioned.
Therefore, the Cabinet Mission was not fully accepted by the Indian National Congress and the Muslim League.

markup: Gandhiji took up the vow of service to India.
answermarkup:
i. Gandhiji returned to India from South Africa on 9th January, 1915.
ii. On the suggestion of Gopal Krishna Gokhale, Gandhiji made a tour of the entire nation.
iii. On his tour, he noticed the poverty and misery of the people. This made him upset. Therefore, Gandhiji took up the vow of service to İndia.

markup: The National Congress split at its Surat session in 1907.
answermarkup:
1) The differences between the moderates and the extremists reached a climax in 1907.
2) The moderates wanted to keep aside the resolution of Swadeshi and Boycott which was thwarted by the extremists.
3) Some moderate leaders blamed the extremist leaders for trying to capture the Indian National Congress.
4) It became impossible to arrive at a compromise between both the groups.
As a result the Indian National Congress split at its Surat session in 1907.

markup: Gandhiji became disappointed in the Second Round Table Conference (1931).
answermarkup:
i. The Second Round Table Conference was organised in 1931 and Mahatma Gandhi attended it as a representative of the Indian National Congress.
ii. Several other representatives of various communities, castes, political parties as well as princely states were also present.
iii. The Government took up the issue of minorities in the Conference. The representatives differed on the issue of minorities and also on the nature of the future Federal constitution.
iv. Gandhiji tried to bring harmony in the opinion but failed to do so.
Therefore, Gandhiji became disappointed in the Second Round Conference (1931) and returned back to India.

markup: The British captured Sindh in 1843.
answermarkup:
1) The British were afraid of Russian aggression Afghanistan. on India via Afghanistan.
2) They decided to bring Afghanistan under their control to ensure safety of their Indian Empire.
3) The province of Sindh was located at North west frontier.
4) All routes to Afghanistan passed through Sindh.
5) Realising its strategic importance, the British captured Sindh in 1843.

markup: All India States People's Conference was formed in 1927.
answermarkup:
i. The influence of the non-co-operation movement led to a political awakening among the princely states.
ii. It further led to the formation of Praja Mandals i.e. people's organisations in these princely states.
iii. These Praja Mandals worked for the interest of the people of the princely states as well as for securing political rights for them.
iv. Various such Praja Mandals came together and formed the 'All India States People's Conference' in 1927, which gave an impetus to the movement in the princely states.

markup: Subhash Chandra Bose resigned from the office of Congress President.
answermarkup:
1) Subhash Chandra Bose became the President of Indian National Congress twice.
(2) He became the President of Congress when Second World War had commenced. He was of the opinion that as England was engaged in war, the Congress should intensify the agitation by taking advantage of this situation.
(3) If needed, India should seek the help of the enemies of England.
(4) Other senior leaders of the Congress did not agree with this view.
As a result, Subhash Chandra Bose resigned from the office of the Congress President.

markup: Merger of the Princely States was essential.
answermarkup:
1) When India got independence there were more than six hundred princely states in India.
(2) If the princely states had remained independent, India would have been split into hundreds of territorial fragments.
(3) The dream of Indian National Congress of undivided India would have remained incomplete.
(4) Moreover, the organisations in the princely states had started movements to secure rights.
(5) It was necessary to free the people from the autocratic rule in the princely states.
(6) Some princely states started carrying out movements for merging with Pakistan.

markup: All India States People's Conference was formed in 1927.
answermarkup:
1) There was political awakening among the people of princely states due to influence of non-co-operation movement.
(2) Praja Mandals were formed to secure the political rights for the people in the Princely states and to work for their interest.
(3) All the Praja Mandals came together and formed an "All India States People's Conference, in 1927 which gave an impetus to the freedom movement.

markup: In November 1939, provincial ministers of Indian National Congress gave their resignations.
answermarkup:
1) Viceroy Lord Linlithgo declared in 1939 that India had joined the Second World War on the side of England, without consulting the Indian leaders.
(2) England claimed that it was fighting to save democracy in Europe.
(3) Thereupon, the Congress claimed that if that claim is true then England should grant Independence to India immediately.
(4) So the provincial ministries of the Indian National Congress resigned in November 1939 as England did not accept this demand.

markup: Rowlatt Act was opposed by the people of India.
answermarkup:
1) The Rowlatt Act was enacted to suppress the growing discontent among the Indians and suggest measures about it.
2) This Act authorised the government to arrest any Indian and imprison him without trial or warrant.
3) There was no provision for appeal against the punishment given under the Act.
4) Due to such unjust provisions in the Rowlatt Act it was opposed by the people of India and called 'Black Act'.

markup: The Cripps proposal was rejected.
answermarkup:
(1) The Indian National Congress rejected the Cripps' proposal because there was no clear mention of the grant of complete independence to India.
(2) The Muslim League rejected the Cripps' proposal as it had no mention of creation of Pakistan.

markup: Gandhiji suspended the Non-co-operation Movement.
answermarkup:
1) In February, 1922 the police opened fire on a peaceful procession at Chauri-Chaura in Gorakhpur district of Uttar Pradesh.
2) In retaliation to this, the enraged mob set fire the police station in Chauri-Chaura.
3) Twenty-two policemen including one officer were killed in this incident.
4) Gandhiji was hurt by this incident. So he decided to suspend the Non-co-operation Movement on 12 February, 1922.

markup: Chandrasing Thakur was court martialled and severely punished.
answermarkup:
1) Khan Abdul Gaffar Khan began Satyagraha at Peshawar on 23rd  April, 1930. His organisation Khuda-i-Khidmatgar led the satyagraha.
(2) They kept Peshawar town in their control for a week.
(3) The British government ordered Garhwal regiment to fire on the satyagrahis.
(4) Chandrasing Thakur an officer of the Garhwal Regiment refused to fire on the satyagrahis.
Therefore, he was court martialled and severely punished.

markup: During the British period, newspapers also acted as source of social reformation.
answermarkup:
1) Newspapers like Amrit Bazaar Patrika, Deenbandhu, Dnyanoday, Kesari, etc. acted as important source to awaken the minds of the people.
2) Newspapers in the British period not only opposed imperialism but also educated the masses and created awareness among the people.
3) The Nibandhmala by Vishnushastri Chiplunkar and Shatapatre written by Lokahitawadi alias Gopal Hari Deshmukh published in the weekly Prabhakar commented on various social and cultural issues.
4) Newspapers threw light on ill customs like sati, child marriage, ban on widow remarriage, etc. and awakened minds of the people.
5) We came to know about various policies of the British towards India and their effects on India.
6) Thus newspapers were not only source of political events but also acted as a source of social reformation.

markup: Khudiram Bose was hanged to death.
answermarkup:
1) Anushilan Samiti worked with the objective to overthrow the British rule with armed rebellion.
(2) Prafulla Chaki and Khudiram Bose were the members of Anushilan Samiti.
(3) They planned to kill α judge named Kingsford.
(4) They threw a bomb at a vehicle, assuming it to be of Kingsford but the vehicle was not the one carrying him.
(5) However, two English women were killed in this attack. Khudiram Bose was caught by the police and was hanged.

markup: The Government declared Martial Law at Solapur.
answermarkup:
1) After the Salt Satyagraha many movements which were integral of Civil Disobedience Movement started.
(2) The mill workers in Solapur observed hartal and organised a huge procession on 6th  May 1930.
(3) The District Collector ordered firing on procession. Many volunteers including Shankar Shivdare died in the firing.
(4) People got enraged and attacked railway stations, police stations, courts, municipal buildings, etc.
Therefore, Martial law was imposed in Solapur by the government.

markup: The Indian National Congress approved the partition.
answermarkup:
1) Lord Mountbatten prepared α plan of creation of India and Pakistan as two independent nations.
(2) Indian National Congress opposed the plan of partition as unity of the Nation was its basic stand.
(3) However, the Muslim League remained adamant on the creation of Pakistan.
(4) So, the Indian National Congress was left with no option but to accept the partition with complete helplessness.

markup: Bhagat Singh, Sukhdev and Rajguru were hanged.
answermarkup:
1) Bhagat Singh and Batukeshwar Dutta threw a bomb in Central Legislative Assembly.
(2) The British Government started arresting the revolutionaries. They immediately raided the centres of 'Hindustan Socialist Republican Army' and got clues related to the killing of Saunders.
(3) Bhagat Singh, Rajguru and Sukhdev were tried under the charge of sedition.
(4) They were hanged in the Lahore jail on 23 March 1931.

markup: The Indian Government took decision of using military force against the Portuguese in Goa.
answermarkup:
i. When Portugal denied the handover of the territories under its possession to India; the Indians had to struggle for securing these territories.
ii. Dr. T. B. Kunha, was in the forefront of this struggle and worked to bring about awakening of the people.
iii. Later, the Goa Mukti Samiti formed in 1954, sent many batches of satyagrahis from Maharashtra to Goa.
iv. The Portuguese rulers committed unlimited tyranny and atrocities on the satyagrahis, which led the public opinion to become more infuriated and the struggle for the liberation of Goa took up a fierce form.
v. Also, the Portuguese government did not respond to the peaceful negotiations held by the Indian government.
This forced the Indian government to make use of military force and in December 1961, the Indian Army entered Goa and made the Portuguese army surrender in a short time.

markup: Audio-visual considered recordings are as the most trustworthy source for the study of Modern Indian History.
answermarkup:
Audio-visual recordings are considered as trustworthy source for study of modern history. Because
1) Important events during the freedom struggle could be seen in reality.
2) Audio-visual recordings of Dandi March, Quit India movement, Salt Satyagraha and other historical events are available.
3) Films also dealt with subjects like social problems, superstitions, practices. They reflect contemporary social, religious. political issues.
Therefore, audio-visual recordings are considered as a unique discovery of 20th century.

markup: The Muslim League was established in 1906.
answermarkup:
The Muslim League was established in 1906 due to the following reasons:
i. The British were worried after seeing the unity of the people and their great response to the Indian National Congress during the Anti-Partition Movement. Hence, they adopted the 'Divide and Rule' policy once again.
ii. They spread the idea that the interests of the Muslims should be safeguarded through a separate political organisation.
iii. To achieve this, a committee of upper class Muslims led by Aga Khan met Governor General Lord Minto.
iv. The Governor General and other British officers motivated the Muslims which led to the formation of Muslim League in 1906.

markup: Two groups were formed in the Congress.
answermarkup:
1) Though at a slow pace, the contribution of Indian National Congress was consistent in the initial stage. But the extremists felt to intensify the freedom struggle.
2) Moderates and Extremists were unanimous about the objectives of Congress. But they had differences regarding the methods/ways to achieve it.
3) The moderates insisted on constitutional measures whereas extremists wanted to adopt severe methods.
4) The tension between these groups increased during the Surat session in 1907.
This led to the formation of two groups within the Congress.

markup: The leaders and the people of Marathwada had a lion's share in the struggle for liberation of Hyderabad.
answermarkup:
i. Valuable contribution was made by Swami Ramananda Tirth, Govindbhai Shroff, Anant Bhalerao, Ashatai Waghmare, etc. in the struggle for the liberation of Hyderabad.
ii. Students participated in this struggle through the 'Vande Mataram' movement.
iii. Also, Ved Prakash, Govind Pansare, Shyamlal, Shridhar Vartak, Bahirji Shinde, Janardan Mama, Shoaib Ullah Khan, etc. embraced martyrdom and inspired other Indians.
Since all these were from the Marathwada part of Hyderabad, it is said that the leaders and the people of Marathwada had a lion's share in the struggle for liberation of Hyderabad.

markup: The movement started by Mill workers at Ahmedabad was successful.
answermarkup:
1) During the First World War the inflation was very high.
2) The mill workers demanded for rise in salary which was refused by the mill owners.
3) Gandhiji advised the workers to go on hunger strike.
4) In the end, the mill owners had to back off and the salary of workers was increased.

markup: There aroused a need of nationwide workers union.
answermarkup:
1) In the later half of the 19th century, textile mills, railway companies and such other industries were started in India.
(2) The workers group were not aroused on large scale.
(3) As there were no unions, the workers were not organised.
(4) After the First World War, there was rise of worker class in India due to industrialisation.
Therefore, a necessity was felt for nationwide worker union.

markup: Junagad merged with India.
answermarkup:
(1) Junagad was a princely state in Saurashtra.
(2) The Nawab of Junagad wanted to merge the state with Pakistan.
(3) It was opposed by the people vigorously as they wanted the merger with India.
(4) Due to this, the Nawab fled to Pakistan and Junagad was merged with India in February, 1948.

markup: The decision of one day token strike was taken on 21st  November 1955.
answermarkup:
i. A grand march was led by Senapati Bapat to Vidhan Bhavan, at a time when the discontent among the Marathi speaking people fighting for Samyukta Maharashtra was growing.
ii. Due to this, the government led by the Chief Minister Morarji Desai declared a ban.
iii. Further, an open meeting was conducted at the Kamgar Maidan, where Comrade Amrut Dange guided a crowd of around 50 thousand people.
iv. The police lathi charged and also used tear gas at the protestors.
v. Thereafter, to accelerate the struggle for the Samyukta Maharashtra Movement a decision to hold one day token strike was taken on 21st  November 1955.

markup: The British imposed heavy taxes on Indian industries.
answermarkup:
1) The British introduced new revenue system with the sole purpose to increase their income.
2) The taxes were forcibly collected from the farmers.
3) British goods were sold in India to gain profits.
4) They imposed heavy taxes on the goods made by local industries.
5) This trade policy ruined Indian handicraft and textile industries.
6) Many artisans became unemployed.
The British imposed heavy taxes on Indian industries with the sole purpose to ruin the Indian economy.

markup: A feeling of nationalism developed among the Indians.
answermarkup:
1) The British established α centralised administration in India and applied uniform policies all over the country.
2) They also laid down the principle of equality before law.
3) They introduced the modern means of transport and communication.
4) It benefited Indians as well. This made possible for the people living in different parts of India to establish contact with one another.
This factors developed a feeling of nationalism among the Indians.

markup: Inspirational songs are an important source of history.
answermarkup:
i. Various types of inspirational songs were composed during the freedom movement.
ii. Some of these songs are available in written form, while many others which were memorised by the freedom fighters remain unpublished.
iii. These songs provide information about the conditions during the pre-independence period.
iv. They also convey the spirit behind the freedom struggle.
Thus, inspirational songs are an importance source of understanding history.

markup: Gandhiji was arrested on 4th  May, 1930.
answermarkup:
i. Gandhiji launched the Civil Disobedience Movement in 1930 by breaking the Salt Act. People all over India responded to it positively.
ii. Khan Abdul Gaffar Khan, the loyal follower of Gandhiji, started satyagraha at Peshawar. For nearly a week, the whole town was in the hands of the Satyagrahis.
iii. Chandrasingh Thakur, an officer of Garhwal Regiment disobeyed the British Government orders of opening fire on the Satyagrahis.
iv. Due to the satyagraha launched by Mahatma Gandhi, the British Government found itself in difficult situation.
Therefore, the British Government arrested Gandhiji on 4th  May, 1930.

markup: The British government suspended the punishment of INA officers.
answermarkup:
1) After surrender of the soldiers of the Indian National Army, the British government charged them with treason.
(2) Expert lawyers like Pandit Nehru, Bhulabhai Desai and Tej Bahadur Sapre defended the INA officers.
(3) But the military tribunal held them guilty and sentenced them to life imprisonment.
(4) There was severe unrest in the minds of the Indian people against the British Government. So, they had to suspend the punishment given by the military tribunal.

markup: The Congress Socialist Party was formed in 1934.
answermarkup:
1) Many young activists of the Indian National Congress believed that the society should be built on the principles of economic and social equality.
(2) Due to this, there was spread of socialist ideas and thoughts.
(3) They believed that to protect interests of the people it was necessary to overthrow the British rule.
(4) So, they decided to set up a Socialist Party within the Congress fold while they were in Nashik jail. Accordingly, the Congress Socialist Party was formed in 1934.

markup: Lokmanya was imprisoned in 1897.
answermarkup:
1) In 1897, hundreds of people died in Pune due to the epidemic of Plague.
2) An officer name Rand was appointed to bring the epidemic under control.
3) He started a search campaign to find Plague patients and adopted oppressive measures.
4) To avenge this cruel and oppressive treatment meted out to people, the Chapekar brothers assassinated him.
5) An unsuccessful attempt was made by the government to connect Lokmanya Tilak with this conspiracy.
6) When they failed in their attempt, they imprisoned him with revenge.

markup: The government passed the Morley-Minto Act.
answermarkup:
1) The economic policies of the British increased poverty in India.
2) It created dissatisfaction in the minds of the people against British rule.
3) The oppressive measures adopted by Lord Curzon to suppress the protest of partition of Bengal, exclusion of educated Indians in government services and the unjust treatment towards Indians in Africa all this added to the dissatisfaction among the Indians.
4) Morley-Minto reforms were passed by the British government as a temporary remedy to calm discontent among the Indians.

markup: The Indian National Army had to lay down their arms.
answermarkup:
1) The Indian National Army fought against the British in adverse circumstances under the leadership of Subhash Chandra Bose.
(2) The Imphal Campaign of Indian National Army remained incomplete as the Japanese stopped helping the Indian National Army.
(3) In the same period, Japan accepted defeat in the Second World War.
(4) On 18 August 1945, Subhash Chandra Bose died in a plane crash.
Under these circumstances, the soldiers of the Indian National Army had to lay down their arms.

markup: The social and religious reform movement began in India.
answermarkup:
1) With the spread of English education in India, there was spread of new ideas, new thoughts, new philosophy.
2) Indians got introduced to western thoughts and culture.
3) They wanted to create a society based on principles of Humanity, Equality and Fraternity.
4) They realised that the flaws like superstitions, casteism, old customs, class system and lack of critical outlook is responsible for the backwardness of India.
5) This association was responsible for social and religious reform in India.

markup: The British government imprisoned Tilak with revenge in 1897.
answermarkup:
i. The epidemic of plague had spread in Pune in 1897 on a large scale. This led to the death of a large number of people.
ii. Officer Rand who was appointed to look into this matter searched the plague patients and adopted oppressive measures against them.
iii. So, the Chapekar brothers assassinated Rand. The British thought that Tilak was involved in this plan.
iv. However, when the government was unsuccessful to connect relation of Lokmanya Tilak with this conspiracy, the British government imprisoned Tilak with revenge.

markup: Maps and drawings are important source of history.
answermarkup:
1) We come to know about changing nature of a city or a location from the map.
2) They are important from the view of study of architecture of a building as well as phases of development of a particular area.
3) The development of Bombay city can be understood through the plans drafted by architects and engineers who made the original plan of Bombay Port Trust.
Therefore, we can say that maps and drawings are important source of history.

markup: Siraj-ud-Daulah was defeated in the Battle of Plassey.
answermarkup:
1) The officers of the British East India Company misused the trade concessions and built fortification around the factory in Kolkata.
2) Siraj-ud-Daulah captured the factory at Kolkata.
3) This created discontent in England.
4) Robert Clive diplomatically bribed Mir Jafar, Commander in Chief of Nawab's army and promised to make him Nawab of Bengal.
5) So, the Army of Siraj-ud-Daulah under the command of Mir Kasim did not join the battle against the British at Plassey in 1757 AD.
6) Thus, the British won the battle of Plassey by treachery and deceit.

markup: Farmers in India became bankrupt.
answermarkup:
The British made number of changes in the existing system to increase the revenue.
1) The payment of revenue was made compulsory in cash and within the prescribed time limit.
2) Land was confiscated if the revenue was not paid in time.
3) The land revenue collection differed from place to place which resulted in the exploitation of the farmers.
4) Farmers were forced to sell their produce to the merchants and middlemen at a low price in order to pay revenue.
5) Farmers mortgaged land to pay tax and became indebted to moneylenders.
In this way, the farmers became bankrupt in India.

markup: Compared to ancient and medieval period, the sources of study of modern Indian history are found in abundance.
answermarkup:
Compared to ancient and medieval period, the sources of study of modern Indian history are found in abundance due to the following reasons:
i. The archaeological sources of the modern period are in a better condition as compared to the sources belonging to ancient and medieval period.
ii. Most of these sources are in written form and are preserved in the archives. However, while using the written sources, the ideology and opinions of the author regarding the particular event should be examined properly.
iii. Also, some sources that belong to the modern period are available in audio, video and audio-visual form. Even these sources are preserved in archives.
iv. As these sources are very important for knowing the various political, social and economic conditions of a particular period, they should be preserved through which the rich and glorious past can be handed over to future generation.

markup: It is required to verify the written sources before they are used.
answermarkup:
1) We have to be careful while making use of written sources. The authenticity of the documents needs to be verified.
2) We need to see the ideas suggested through them.
3) Before making use of the document it is necessary to know the perspective of the writer, his ideologies and opinions about a particular event.
4) If all the angles are not considered the writings become one-sided.
Hence it is necessary to verify written sources.

markup: Bhagat Singh and Batukeshwar Dutta threw bombs in the Central Legislative Assembly.
answermarkup:
1) The Government had introduced two bills in the Central Legislature.
(2) The Bills curtailed civil rights of the people.
(3) To protest against these bills, Bhagat Singh and Batukeshwar Dutta threw bombs in the Central Legislative Assembly.

markup: Many organisations were formed in the Hyderabad Princely State.
answermarkup:
1) There were Telugu, Kannada and Marathi speaking regions in princely state of Hyderabad.
(2) There was absence of civil and political rights under the autocratic rule of the Nizam.
(3) To secure these rights organsiatons were formed in the princely states of Hyderabad.
